And what rank has not benefited from his regulations? He laid down laws for youth and old age, for slaves and free people, that they should submit to one Lord.

He brought every rank under the rule of his preaching and yoked men together with their wives in the yoke of love. He gave victory to the determined striving of the righteous, and strengthened and supported the weakness of those who had fallen. He ordered the ranks of authority, both inside and outside, and showed everyone how to render what was due. He yoked the world with the gentle yoke of its Lord’s love, so that everyone might labor at the task of spiritual life. He drove the darkness of evil’s power away from humanity and urged people toward the light of his preaching. With the sword of his word he cut down the love of gain and cast it away, and showed everyone the bitterness hidden in its fruits. With the spear of his love he demolished the heights of the love of glory, and humbled the pride and arrogance that accompany a person. Envy is a snake that chews its venom and kills people. He shot into it the arrow of the word of peace, and its venom lost its strength. He called to the angry, “Come, be calm and leave off your anger before the sun of life, which measures out your time, goes down.” He set fear and the sentence of judgment before sinners, then turned and encouraged them: if they become righteous, they will not be condemned. He revealed the wealth of the kindness of the God of all, which he will display at the end of the ages toward all and in all. “Oh,” he said, “the depth of the great, boundless wealth that sustains the world and its inhabitants without being diminished!” Oh, the discernment whose searching penetrates the senses and impulses, from which not even a glance or a slight gesture escapes! Oh, the knowledge that enclosed everything in ignorance, so that it might give life and graciously bring the work of its hands to life! O mighty man, to whom the command gave [?] the keys of the Spirit, and who opened [?] the treasury of hidden things [?] concealed from everyone! O disciple who reached the rank of teacher, who through meditation learned and taught the three Persons! O you who were trained by the Law for the kingdom on high, who became rich and enriched the people and the nations from its treasures!

In you the power of wonders was fulfilled through deeds, for you embraced the riches of the Law and of the Spirit. You deserve to be called blessed by every mouth, O herald, for you proclaimed the truth and turned everyone toward reverence for the truth. May a crown of victory be offered to you by every tongue, for you taught people to sing praise to the name of the divine Being. All ranks ought to walk along the path of your words, for you opened the way to the resurrection of the body and the liberation of the soul. Let those who love the truth build upon the structure of your teaching, for you built and completed one unshakable confession of faith. Let everyone turn toward your goal in body and soul, for you died to creation, and creation itself was dead to you. Every day you were crucified to desires, as though you were not alive, and you regarded the living world as something dead. Blessed are you, Paul, obedient one, who were persuaded and persuaded others, for a crown of victory is reserved for you for the contest of your labors. Join us in pleading, obedient one, as you are accustomed to do, so that we may be found worthy of mercy when the divine command finds you worthy of blessings. Response: Give thanks to the Merciful One, who teaches ways of compassion to those who love his righteousness.
On the Apostles

Homily 8. On the Apostles. His own is finished, while it is his own [?]. The eighth homily, which he composed on all the apostles, and which is recited at the commemoration of the evangelists. Response: Blessed is Christ, who clothed his apostles in the armor of the Spirit, through which they conquered and triumphed. Another: Blessed is Christ, who pledged and promised a reward to the righteous and judgment to the wicked. My brothers.

The King on high prepared a spiritual banquet and sent his servants to invite everyone to the wedding feast of his love. He invited and called the heavenly and earthly beings, and sent his servants to invite everyone to the wedding feast of his love. He invited and called the heavenly and earthly beings, and prepared spiritual food that does not perish. He seated them at table in the temple of the visible body and showed them the power of his greatness through things plainly perceptible to the senses. He placed the crown of divinity on the head of the Son of Man, so that human beings [?] spiritual beings might see the hidden one openly. You could not see the Son and gaze upon him. Therefore he displayed his glory in the body before the eyes of those who saw him. He displayed his glory before the eyes of his creatures, not his essence; he revealed the power of his greatness to his works, not his hidden nature. The Will clothed the Word that came from him in bodily garments, and through him expressed the power of the revelation of his secrets. His love fashioned a spiritual harp of flesh, so that through it he might gladden spiritual and bodily beings. His will struck the strings of the body as though with a finger, and human beings and spiritual beings marveled at the sweetness of his voice. Beautiful was the wedding feast that the hidden one prepared for the work of his hands, and very sweet was the song of his hidden nature on the flute of flesh. He prepared a banquet for the work of his hands, not for his grace, for he has no need: his blessedness belongs to his very being. He honored his image through what he revealed about his being. He made no addition to his nature through the things he acquired. He cannot grow greater or become less than what he is, nor does his nature acquire joy or sorrow through the things that are revealed. He wished to renew rational beings through what he did, and through them in turn expressed the power of the wisdom of his hidden love. He honored the likeness of his image above everything, as befits an image, and through it brought joy to the gloom that had driven peace away. Human sin disturbed peace and dissolved love, and through human beings he wished to reconcile everyone with his love. His will chose one from among human beings and called him by his own name, and through him turned rational beings toward the knowledge of him. He called the affection of his love a banquet, which he prepared for his honor [?].

He gathered the heavenly and earthly beings to him. He called those of his own race servants and messengers, and invited everyone to the wedding feast of spiritual life. His command spoke in a tongue of flesh with bodily beings and taught them how to catch human beings for life [?]. His power strengthened the weakness of your minds, so that they might bring peace to the divided world through the sound of their words. He compounded his love like medicine with their words, so that through their sayings they might heal the afflictions of body and soul. He clothed your minds with his truth as with armor, so that they might overcome the error that the Evil One sowed in the [?] of humanity. Compassionate mercy anointed their impulses like athletes, so that the hand of demons might trip them in the contest of hardships. He put the sword of the Spirit into their hands to destroy wickedness, so that the enemy might be put to shame and the people he had killed might kill him. He clothed them with the strength of his help as with coats of armor, so that the arrows of his deceit would not lodge in their limbs. He put faith into their hands like a shield, so that with it they might protect body and soul from harm. He equipped them spiritually for various kinds of combat, so that they would know how to join battle against terrors. With everyone and in everything, he kept them occupied in the exercise of hardships, and through experience they gained training in spiritual things. They learned from the Spirit the power of the wisdom of every craft; he grew rich and enriched the poor from their treasures. Their deeds became light and salt in creation. They enlightened the sluggish and gave flavor to those who were tasteless. They drove error away with the glorious [?] of their conduct and made the light of righteousness shine amid the darkness. They uprooted paganism, the false structure that demons had built, and established truth, the pure truth of the Creator’s name. They demolished the shrines of idolatry that demons had adorned, and perfected love and faith in human minds. They drove the thick darkness of the name of gods away from all nations, and the world saw the beautiful radiance of the one God. Their voices became like thunder among the inhabitants of earth. Those who were sunk down stirred, and the sluggish rose at the sound of their words. Their impulses spiritually took hold of the net of love. They spread it over everyone, and it caught both good and evil people from among them all. They caught rational prey from the sea and caught it from dry land, and [?] them like an offering to the King on high. The King himself also called his proclamation a net, which his love spread over all nations through the hands of his servants. Through their deeds the apostles fulfilled that utterance: “Make disciples and baptize all nations in the name of the divine Being.” They received three names from him like a seal, and they sealed people and stamped them spiritually. They marked the Trinity upon their impulses and their limbs, so that everyone might learn to hallow the name worthy of worship. With the living mark they branded the flock of humankind, gathered it together, and brought it into the fold of spiritual life. They fed the rational sheep on the pasture of the Spirit, and he settled them beside springs of peaceful refreshment.

They [?] properly, maintained order, and cared for them wisely; they taught the lambs and ewes wisdom through love of the truth. They tended those who were sick, bound up those who were broken, and sought those who were lost. They nourished and guarded the whole flock as one body. Like a mirror, that saying addressed to Simon, “Do you love?” was always fixed before their minds. [?] Through great love, the shepherds of the flock [?] his will; out of love for humanity, they hastened to sufferings, even to death. They loved humanity more than everything, as they had been commanded; and for humanity they [?] their lives and loved death. They honored humanity because of the love of the one who loves humanity, for they saw that he loved humanity [?] more than everything. They saw that in his love he willingly put on the likeness of a servant, to raise humanity from lowly [?] to greatness. Those called by his name imitated his love and loved humanity, and taught people to turn to him along the path of truth. According to his [?], they pounded medicine for their diseases and gave them compassion and mercy to drink, so that they would not be worn down. With mercy they healed the sick who had long suffered the pains of wrongdoing, and with compassion they bandaged the dead whom the Evil One had [?]. They applied compassion to the wounds of the senses and impulses, and washed them in the gentle waters of baptism. They brought body and soul in as into a furnace and smelted them, and scoured from them the hateful filth of hateful wrongdoing. Like potters, they shattered the rational vessels and renewed them through repentance into a fresh mass of clay. O mortals, whose nature is clay, [?] to breaking, who refashioned and renewed their limbs and became gold! O earthly ones, children of dust, despised in its appearance, who gave humanity in its lowliness the body of heavenly beings! O poor ones, whose father incurred a debt and sold them, who bought the world with the wealth they gathered through their labors! He grew rich from the treasury of the one honored with the name of Creator; and they enriched humanity with what was not theirs as though it were their own. With what was not theirs, they freed their own from slavery and drew up for them a charter of freedom without [?]. They received the armor of the spirit from the spiritual King, and with it they triumphed before spiritual and bodily beings. They rescued captive humanity from death and from Satan, and freed them from enslavement to the service of wrongdoing. They fought against the mighty one who had enslaved humanity, and took from him the captives he had carried away from their ranks. With the sword of the Spirit they surrounded the enemy’s camp and brought down the ranks of his armies before bodily beings. The mighty one who had enslaved humanity was defeated, and humanity triumphed; the demons cried out at the voice of people clothed in the Spirit. 50. In the spirit, spiritual beings fought with bodily beings, and people clothed in suffering defeated those not subject to suffering. Endurance worked a great wonder through the love of the righteous, for they [?] the visible body against the spirit. Glorious is the struggle they displayed on earth through their labors, and the mouth is too small to recount the story of their victories.

The course of their lives is longer than can be measured, and the mind is [?] to journey with them to the end. Fearsome is the contest in which they struggled against threats, and the heart is apprehensive about recounting their sufferings. The passage read about them is full of fear and [?]. Their labors are fearsome; their crowns are glorious. Blessed is the one who loves! Through love the mind can read about their deeds, and love shows the one who loves the path of their labors. Through faith his mind can be strengthened by them, and faith encourages him not to let go of what has been promised. Hope urges the hidden mind toward hidden things, and strengthens it to trample sufferings underfoot through endurance. The victorious clothed themselves in love, hope, and faith, and with these they fought against all fierce foes, hidden and visible. They armed themselves with these as with weapons against the Evil One, and through them they fought against spiritual and bodily beings. Relying on their support, they entered the contest of harsh labors, trampling sufferings underfoot and despising [?] as though they were not human. By what they did, they made their love resemble that of beings beyond suffering. They hated life and loved death, contrary to custom. Beyond the ordinary order, they despised [?] and its bondage. They came to hate earthly things and loved the things above. They loved the things above, though these were entirely hidden from sight, and hated the things below, though these were plainly apparent to the senses and impulses. Out of loving desire for rich things, they despised what was on earth and taught people to hate earthly things. Hidden things were before their eyes like visible things, and [?] them like a mirror before [?]. They showed them to earthly beings as though pointing with a finger: “Look, mortals, and see the beauty hidden on high!” They enticed people toward the promised things as though they were children, and nourished them with spiritual food as though with milk. They sprinkled the medicine of life upon the earth of mortality, and the dead began to live [?] at the sound of their words. Mortals heard new sounds [from mortals]: people proclaiming in human ears the abolition of death. Human beings brought humanity new good news: the resurrection of the body, the salvation of the soul, and the renewal of everything. They awakened human beings as though from sleep, and those sunk in slumber stirred at the announcement of the renewal of body and soul. They taught everyone to utter the name of the divine Being: three persons who are not divided by difference. Uneducated men wrote a new book for rational beings; they taught them how to read “Father,” “Son,” and “Spirit.” They wrote three names on the tablets of their minds: one Being whose everlasting existence has no beginning. They depicted in ink the nature that clothed itself in a body, so that people might read of the Word and the body, the hidden in the visible. They depicted the likeness of the servant and of the Maker among the written lines,

so that everyone might see the image of what is hidden through the outward senses. Their voices sang of divinity together with humanity, and their song gladdened spiritual and bodily beings. They called one offspring the Son of the divine Being and the Son of humanity: one from the height and one from the depth, the Word and the body. They proclaimed the hidden and the visible, and taught human beings to gain hope through the visible toward the divine Being. At the body's gate [?], they confined the senses and impulses, so that they would not wear themselves out searching for the Hidden One who cannot be comprehended. They fashioned bodily existence in their hands like a mirror, and showed the world the power of hidden reality through the visible senses. They inscribed God's name on a bodily tablet, and gave the human being a divine name. They called the divine Being and humanity “God-man,” the Son of God, whose love dwelt in the temple of our body. The hidden Spirit revealed to them the mysteries of [?], and they proclaimed them: two [?], one person. He himself revealed to them hidden mysteries they had not known, and taught them how to confess the Word and the body. They distinguished the natures from one another as they are, so that the nature of the divine Being would not be diminished by our body, which he put on. They duly assigned to each what belonged to it, so that everyone might learn that the Self-existent One is not mingled with our body. They attributed to the Self-existent One separation from all things, as befits him, and called the body visible, as it is. They exalted the One who cannot suffer and placed him above sufferings, and clothed the mortal one in the garment of mortality. As knowledgeable men, they distinguished and harmonized the two, so that those traveling along the path of their sayings would not become confused. They were afraid that someone might stray from the truth, and that the runner might fall short in the race [?] of the perfection of the Creator's name. They were concerned for the cultivation of spiritual life, lest the thicket of error sprout among the good seed. They were very careful in building love and faith, lest deceitful workers build with straw and stubble. With a hidden eye they examined things to come: that people would arise who would tear down the truth and build falsehood. It was revealed to them that wolves would take on the likeness of sheep and bite people's [?] under their disguises. They perceived the evil inclination of the heretics, who would soil the beautiful garment of faith. They saw that people were going to do wrong to the body that came from us, and they uprooted beforehand the hateful thicket of their thoughts. They first sowed the name “humanity” in people's ears, and [?] and [?] concerning the divine Being who is hidden from all. Wisely learn the revealed truth: the hidden will and the bodily temple, two that became one. They led them step by step from lowly things to glorious things, for this is what the proper order prescribes for anyone who teaches. They gave people bodily existence to drink like milk, and then offered them the wondrous food of divinity. The fishermen spread these [?] throughout creation.

They enclosed the world in the nets of their sayings. By these means they cultivated the earth that was full of thorns, and its bosom brought forth fruits of praise for the one who fashioned it. The spiritual farmers sowed these words, and the crop of their faith flourished in the soil of humanity. This is the path that the guides of faith blazed, and angels and human beings began traveling toward the gathering of peace. With these words human beings made peace with the spiritual beings, and engaged them in the good contemplation of a life-giving mind. By this power they prevailed in the struggle against Satan and exposed the mysteries that demons had taught human beings. With this help they triumphed and were crowned, in secret and openly, and [?] the rank of mastery in both worlds. They put on the Creator’s name like armor and fought against everything. They measured the height and everything opposite the abyss. Their movements, together with their bodies, traveled to every region. They healed diseases, raised the dead, and drove out demons. They divided the nations and cities among themselves for their labors, so that each of them might demonstrate his proven worth through his deeds. They set out on the assurance of the voice that had chosen them: “Behold, I am with you forever.” Simon proclaimed among the Romans the new good news: the divinity that clothed itself in a body to give life to all. The fisherman went out first to catch the nations. He cast his net and caught the mother of cities. The chief of the disciples caught the city of supremacy, brought it in, and enclosed it within the fortresses of faith. The firstborn who [?] and confessed of the Son that he is the Son of God was the first to offer the sacrifices of the nations’ conversion. He laid his confession like a stone at the foundation of the house, and built up and completed the nations, joined together by the bonds of love. He stood there in Rome, and the structures of idolatry shook. The error with which demons had adorned the false building fell. At his voice, demons and the human beings who worshiped demons trembled. They despised the worship of those called gods and honored the truth. John too thundered with his voice to the Ephesians and awakened them, as if from sleep, to the service of life. The sound of his voice was like thunder over a barren land, and he watered its bosom with the living rain of the word of his mouth. He cast into it the good seed of faith. Through his deeds he fulfilled the name by which he was called. He made the sound of his proclamation heard like thunder. With the thunder of his voice he raised the dead who had died in sin. He showed them the new way that brought the dead to life. Matthew taught the Trinity among the Hebrews. He sealed the words of prophecy with his proclamation and confirmed them through the promises made to the righteous. He made known to them that the mysteries had been fulfilled and the truth had dawned. He gladdened Abram because the nations had become brothers sharing in his love, and made David rejoice because the king of whom it was written had arisen from his descendants. He recorded his conception, which took place through the Spirit without sexual union, and how he sprang up like a root from Mary, the thirsty ground.

He showed that the hidden Will dwelt in the temple of the body, and called him by the name “Son of God,” who is exalted above all. Luke too, the physician of the spirit, agreed with this purpose, and with his words, as with medicine, healed the Egyptians. A skilled physician was sent to the sick people to bind up their wounds with divine medicines. By God's [?], the son of Shem visited the son of Ham, the slave, and applied to his mind the medicine that frees the soul. The offspring of insolent Ham lay sick with wrongdoing. The Hebrew entered, treated him with the Spirit, and covered his wrongdoing. He released him from the yoke of slavery to wrongdoing and curses [?], and sealed him with the Spirit so that he might be a servant [?] of the King on high. His voice was beautiful [as he cried out in the land of Egypt and silenced the voices] of error through his proclamation. The flow of words from his mouth was far greater than the Gihon, and the stirrings of his soul surpassed those who were silent. His voice was far more terrifying to the Egyptians than the Gihon, and the terrors that accompanied him were greater than Israel's. Moses freed and brought back his people, who had died in sin, and Luke freed and brought back his people with hope and life. The Hebrew promised freedom and life to his own people, and pledged to them the resurrection of the body and the salvation of the soul. Mark nurtured the seed that Peter [?] among the Romans, and with his words he watered the rational fruits with the sweetness of voices. He built his teaching on the chosen confession of Peter, and it was not shaken by the surging winds [?] of error. The truth of his words shone like the sun among the Romans and drove away the darkness of the sorcery that Simon taught. He exposed and revealed that deceiver's craft, and softened his bitterness through the sweetness of the name of Jesus. He uprooted his weeds and cleared away the forest of his death, and sowed among people the good seed of his faith. He began and ended in faith, like his companions, and added his book to the testament of his fellow workers. Through four scribes the King sealed his proclamation, and seventy-eight lent a hand in the salvation of the nations. Like a garment, he spread his teaching throughout the four regions, and they covered the naked world with the garment of [?]. They took the name of Christ in their hands and [?]; and as with a seal [?], they sealed people with it against harm. Though they were many, they regarded one another as a single body, and bound the love of their minds to Christ, the head. Beautiful was the gathering of the members of the Christians, and greatly cherished was the honored name they bore. Christ was depicted like an image before their minds, and they took pride in the imprint of his name as though it were a crown. There was nothing before their eyes except Christ, and on him the hidden gaze of their minds was fixed. They considered life in this age to be nothing, and did not think there was any profit in earthly things.

Paul, the chosen one, the friend of the King on high, was dead while alive and alive while dead, despised and glorious [?]. He was dead to the world, for he took no delight in its pleasures, and he lived in the hope of that renewal which will take place at [?]. He longed insatiably for communion with his Lord and waited to see him with a face free from shame. For he was with him mystically during this present life, but he yearned to be with him completely. The heralds of the Word of Life loved this communion. Though they were on earth, they were not on earth but beside him. For love of him they left everything and honored his love, and they became witnesses to his proclamation among humanity. They proclaimed his conception and made known his birth and his bodily growth. They described his suffering and portrayed his resurrection: he rose and ascended. They heard the voice that commanded them, “Make disciples and baptize.” They lovingly taught his love—the word of his mouth—in everyone's hearing. They went out to the hedges and crossroads in search of people. They gathered both good and bad and filled the banquet hall. They seated them at the spiritual table. They gave them the medicine of life to drink in the mystery of the blood. They nourished them mystically with the body and blood. So that everyone might learn that the body and blood belong to the one who took a body, they accustomed the greedy nations to spiritual food. They despised the folly [?] of idolatry and honored the truth. They clothed the naked in a robe of glory. They restrained the course of their dissolute conduct. He strengthened them in hope and life concerning the promises. He taught them not to grow weak amid the sufferings of this present time. They set the promise of life before their eyes like a target, so that they might look in faith toward the things to come. They urged them to strive to follow his example, and they themselves began like teachers before their pupils. They themselves entered the arena of struggles ahead of the athletes, and they showed the combatants the ways of fighting. They overcame every power through the strength of divine help. They scorned and despised the arrogance of demons and human beings. They despised battles and trampled on the threats of tyrannical kings. They mocked and laughed at judges and their authority. They dismantled the teaching that error had written [?] through human hands, and they wrote books containing the one teaching of the God of all. Their voices were beautiful as they cried out among those on earth: “The Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit are one being.” The music of their spiritual lyres [?] was delightful as they sang: “The Word and the flesh are the Son of God.” Their words were sweet to the angels and to human beings as they sowed the new good news that brought peace. The heavenly assemblies marveled [?] at the power within them, as they overcame every teaching through the power of Jesus.

The spiritual beings stood in amazement at their struggles, for they saw that the world and its might had been brought low by fishermen. They saw that they were clothed in a nature of corruptible flesh, and they marveled greatly at how they overcame the passions within them. O fleshly beings who despised nature and its bondage, and through their endurance displayed the likeness of beings who cannot suffer! O earthly ones who lived in the land of bodily infirmity and were not stained by the ugly pains of its decay! O merchants who traveled a road full of danger and were not robbed of the great treasure of their thoughts! O sailors who sat in a ship on a turbulent sea, whose faith did not drown among the waves! O lyres singing daily to the Trinity, whose thoughts’ strings never lost their harmony! O athletes who engaged in battle with terrors, whose captors’ hands did not grow weary upon their limbs! O farmers who sowed life among mortals and weeded out paganism, the thicket that demons had made grow among human beings! O disciples who kept their love for Christ the Teacher, whose loving gaze never turned away from their Lord! Love is inadequate to recount the story of your thoughts, and the mind cannot paint a picture of your victories. The tongue falls short of reaching the height to which you ascended, and the imagination is too slow to reach the harbor of life with you. Only one can paint the picture of your love, and he knows how to count the labors of your contests. It is clear to him how much you suffered for his love, and he knows how to reward your willing resolve. You labored in his vineyard from the beginning of his [?], and he gives you in return the denarius of life that does not perish.
For the Commemoration of Saint Stephen

Discourse [?]. For the Commemoration of Saint Stephen. Response: Glorious is your death, firstborn of the martyrs. Stephen, friend of Jesus, you who opened a road for the blessed martyrs to follow you to the kingdom on high! My brothers.

The King on high, who conquered the Evil One and death through the wood, chose a soldier for himself and sent him ahead of his army. The champion went out ahead of the army and stood between the troops of the King on high and the adversary. The King sent Stephen ahead of his army so that he would be the first to engage in battle with the rebel. The King sent him in the wondrous rank of the [?], so that when the heavenly powers saw him, they would be stirred by him. He anointed him with the Spirit and equipped him with armor so that he would not be defeated, and ahead of the company of apostles he triumphed in the contest. The King gave him all the armor of warriors so that he could do battle with rebels without fear. The command of the one who sent him placed the sword of the Spirit in his hand, so that he might destroy and cast down the wicked who rebelled against righteousness. He held faith, the shield of truth, in his hands, and with it he intercepted the sharp arrows of his enemies. Whenever they shot arrows of wickedness to mock him,

he caught them with the shield of hope and was not harmed. He wrapped the breastplate of righteousness around his limbs, so that they would not strike him and he would not become a laughingstock to their armies. He put on the helmet of life-saving salvation that the King had given him, to shelter within it his faith, the head of his life. He was entirely girded with faith, and there was no place in it left bare of righteousness. He regarded faith as the head of his life, and he concealed it beneath the helmet so that they would not strike it. The King admonished him and his companions and commanded them, saying, “Be like serpents in your shrewdness.” The serpent is wise: it guards itself against being struck, for while its head lives, it is not destroyed by blows. “In this same way you must guard your faith, for while it is protected, you need not fear injuries.” The zealous soldier held fast to this command and guarded it like his head, lest [?] be harmed. He held faith in his hand like a shield, and put the readiness of the gospel on his feet like shoes. He [?] upon the word of holiness as upon a horse, and upon the humility of righteousness, swift-winged. He rode upon the word, grasped the sword, and clothed himself in truth. He put on the helmet and shod his feet with his Lord’s readiness. He shouted in the enemy’s camp like a commander, and they began trembling at the sound of his voice, which was like thunder. The King sent him ahead of the ranks of the heavenly armies, to blaze a trail for his companions so that they might follow his example. He was the first to blaze the trail of martyrdom for his Lord, and he became the firstborn of the martyrs of Jesus, the King on high. The armies of the ruler of the air were tormented when they saw the warrior who was mocking them. They saw that they were too weak to fight against his strength, so they hired and brought in the descendants of Abram to join them.

The descendants of Abraham and the armies of the Evil One became a single troop to condemn Stephen, the soldier of truth. The descendants of Abraham hired themselves out to the enemy, and received the coming judgment as the wages of their service. Through the Hebrews the Evil One fought against the soldier, just as through their leaders he had fought against the King. Stephen was full of power and grace, and, it is said, he also performed signs in the land of Judah. Men arose—the wicked assembly of the Freedmen, and the Cyrenians with their companions—to dispute with him. The enemies of truth could not stand their ground, even for a little while, against the Spirit who spoke through him. They were defeated by the good soldier’s words and put to shame, and now their condemnation is proclaimed throughout all generations. In their stubbornness they sent men and taught them to say, “We heard him speaking blasphemously against God and against the King.” They seized him and brought him into the midst of the assembly of evildoers, to put him to death as someone who had blasphemed against God. With the arrows of his words, Jesus' witness scourged the descendants of [?], who were not heirs to Abram's hope. The righteous man recounted to Abram's descendants how the divine command had chosen Abram among the Babylonians, to put them to shame. “The divine command,” he said, “chose Abram's descendants from all the nations and honored them above everyone else by making them members of his household. He allowed no one to oppress or harm them, and he delivered them from the Egyptians and the Babylonians. You stiff-necked people, uncircumcised in your hearts! You have opposed him and the Holy Spirit who comes from him. The zeal of your minds resembles that of your ancestors, who persecuted the upright and killed the righteous whom the divine command sent.”

With these words he struck them as though with a rod, and stirred them to bitterness that would not be reconciled. The gall of fury surged in their hearts, and they could not withstand the sharp arrows of his words. The good worker condemned those who worked at the Evil One's snares, and they were embittered because they had taken the side of guilt. They glared in anger as righteousness condemned them. They seized him, took him outside the city, and began stoning him. They could not withstand the love in the words of truth's champion, and they found a way to put him to a temporary death. The victorious man died a temporary death, not an everlasting one, and for this reason he welcomed death with joy. He had learned from his Lord, who had conquered death and broken its sting; therefore he made light of it and was not afraid. He pleaded with the Lord who had chosen him on behalf of those stoning him, asking him not to hold against them this sin they were committing against him. The worker of truth was imitating the Lord of all, who entreated his Father to forgive those who crucified him. The workers of wickedness arranged their ranks as though for battle, and instead of weapons they armed themselves with stones and rocks. The steadfast servant did not weaken because of their wickedness, nor did he shrink from the struggle against injustice. The King who had chosen him encouraged him not to weaken, and opened heaven's veil before him so that he would take fresh courage. Through a vision he saw the heavens opened, and he saw Jesus standing at the right hand. The chosen witness saw Christ standing, standing like someone who wanted to come down to him. In this form Christ showed himself to him, like someone who wanted to come and rescue him from their hands. The champion saw Jesus' indescribable love: he showed himself not seated, but standing. This is how those who care for their loved ones behave: they cannot bring themselves to neglect them when they are being wronged. The King's friend was being scourged by insolent men. The King saw his friend being beaten and showed himself.

Through a vision he showed himself to his beloved friend, and his friend's face shone like the face of an angel of light. The champion saw the light of his glory in the arena, and his eyes shone as he gazed at the kingdom on high. The friend of Jesus was gazing at the kingdom on high, and for this reason he scorned and despised all suffering. The light of Jesus’ radiance was poured over his face, and the light of his soul mingled with the radiance of his face. The light of his face was mingled with the radiance of Jesus’ light, and the light of our Lord’s glory and his own became one. Christ was on high and Stephen among those on earth, and the glory of his Lord on high and his own below were one. He was not like his Lord in indescribable glory. His Lord gave him a portion of his glory, and he became glorious. The King on high clothes his servants in glory on high, but he clothed Stephen in glory while he was on earth. While he was on earth, he gave him the glory of the immortals, to confirm what is to happen at the end. “When our lowly body is transformed,” Paul says, “he will make it like the splendor of his glorious body.” In this same way he acted toward Stephen even now: while he was on earth, he honored his face with his own radiance. Oh, what a wonder was displayed in Stephen! Death was roaring, but he was mocking its cries. Who has ever seen a dying man whose face rejoiced as Stephen rejoiced while he was dying? What warrior had his [?] shine at the time of battle, except this warrior of truth, who was found worthy of this? Who has seen arms raised with stones in them, yet made his face shine and astonished his killers? They all looked intently at him, as it is written—the whole assembly—and marveled at the appearance of his face, wondering what this was.

The workers of wickedness became enraged at the sight of his face and brought down a rain of stones upon him, as upon Abel. Envy stoned him with stones of fury, as it did Abel, and the champion’s blood truly cried out better things than Abel’s. His brother’s envy stoned Abel unjustly, and Stephen’s brothers stoned him unjustly. They gathered a dark cloud of angry stones over the victorious one and buried him beneath them, like Abel, whom Cain killed. Cain killed his brother Abel and buried him beneath stones, raising a heap of stones over him so that he would not be discovered. They too acted in this same way against the innocent man, and like Cain they now await their recompense. Alas for the valiant man who was not [?] with honor, whose radiant body was battered beneath a heap of stones! Alas for you, head that had been consecrated by the laying on of hands, yet unjustly bore a crown of stones through wickedness! He had been consecrated by the laying on of apostolic hands, but the wicked, in their insolence, covered him with stones. The Spirit hovered over him and consecrated him by the power of his overshadowing, but the wicked drenched his body in his own lifeblood. The blessed company of the apostles laid its hands on him and appointed him to be [?] a consecrator of the holy mysteries. He was a minister of the awesome, divine mysteries, and in his ministry he portrayed the likeness of the angels. Deacons possess this likeness in the holy Church, as through their ministry they resemble the powers on high. The champion attained this rank in this earthly life—a rank and appearance that made him truly an angel in the flesh. A nature of flesh and a face of fire could be seen—a wonderful sight in a human nature resembling the angels. For this reason his Lord honored him with the radiance of the angels, so that when he rises from the dead, he will have glory like theirs. The body of the children of light resembles the body of our Lord in that way of life in which mortality is exalted.

The evildoers were not frightened by the light of his face, but in their stubbornness they brazenly stoned the righteous man. The wicked servants who were in my beloved’s vineyard saw the branch that had sprouted on the vine and cut it off in anger. The insolent men saw a branch bearing good fruit and immediately cut it off so that it would not bear sweet fruit. My beloved’s vineyard is the people of the house of Israel, and the wicked servants are the heirs who mocked the owner of the [?]. The owner of the vineyard sent his son to bring back fruit, but they seized him, threw him out of the vineyard, and unjustly killed him. The unjust men pronounced a just judgment when they were asked, “What should the owner of the vineyard do to those servants?” They said that he should utterly destroy those wicked servants who beat his servants, insulted his workers, and killed his son. And the Creator, seeing that the vineyard bore no fruit, broke down its hedge, uprooted its tower, and withheld its water. He withheld prophecy, from which they had drunk the water of the Spirit, and the watchful protection of his providence that had surrounded it. He uprooted the tower—the holy temple that he had built within it, where they used to press out the mute sacrifices prescribed in the Law. He took one vine from the stock of this vineyard and left all the rest to bear brushwood and thorns. The Creator took a vine of life from this vineyard, so that anyone who wished might nourish his soul with the life that comes from it. The firstfruits of our race became a vine of life in the world, to intoxicate his servants with the sweetness of the wine of his love. “I am the true vine,” he said, “and you are the branches.

I have appointed you in the world to go and bring forth glorious fruit. The Father,” he said, “is the cultivator of this vineyard, and every branch on which no fruit is found he takes away. Take care not to neglect bearing good fruit, lest you burn like branches that burn in the fire. A branch that withers is immediately gathered up and thrown into the fire. So it will be with you too, if you do not remain in love for me.” “I am the vine, and you are the branches, and my Father is the gardener. Bear fruit and give thanks, so that you will not be cut off.” The good Lord said these things to the servants he had chosen, and warned them not to stray from his love. They too firmly planted their love in him, like a branch whose root is set in the vine. From its life, life flowed into their planting, and they drank from the waters of its holiness. They grew tall above all the peoples of the earth and sheltered them from the sickness of mortality. They cast shade in every region across the earth and protected them from the blazing heat of sinfulness. All the sweet clusters of their conduct ripened, and everyone ate, and their palates, which had been bitter, became sweet. Everyone’s palate had been bitter from deadly poison, and they sweetened it with the good hope of the resurrection of the dead. He entrusted them with proclaiming the resurrection of the dead on earth: everyone will rise from the dead, just as he rose. The chosen one was planted in this vine like his companions, and the workers of wickedness cut him off with the sickle of their insolence. He firmly grafted himself into this vine with great love, brought forth early fruit, and bore leaves for the healing of humanity. He fed them teachings as food and healed them of their pains through the power of the Spirit. Like his companions, he received fruit from the watering of life, and his leaves rejoiced in a great, indescribable wonder.

The cluster of his soul was full of the wine of Jesus’ love, and those who hated him without cause saw his beauty and became embittered. They became messengers of the devil, the enemy of humanity, and gathered over him a cloud of wrath and a hailstorm of stones. They battered the sweet fruit with a hailstorm of stones, so that those in need of drink would not delight in its sweetness. They put the righteous man inside the winepress of envy and trampled him with the heels of hostility. They splashed his blood like wine inside the winepress and pressed his body beneath the stones like grape pulp. As they carried the stones of wrath that they were throwing at him, Christ’s blood had not been washed from their hands. The Savior’s blood was being defiled on their fingertips as they struck him with the stones of wickedness in their hands. Like wolves, they rushed at the shepherd and tore his body apart. They directed their assault against the Most High, to condemn him. The unclean were not satisfied with having shed the Lord’s blood, and they again became greedy to shed the blood of his beloved friend. They were stained with drops of the Lord’s blood as they came to condemn the beloved lamb. The evening wolves were drunk with blood beyond measure, and their fury was far more bitter than that of wolves. They accepted the Lord’s blood upon themselves and upon their children, and they are stained with it forever, without end. The wicked mixed the servant’s blood with his Lord’s blood, and took it upon themselves as a rebuke to their guilt. The holy man’s blood was immersed in the likeness of his Lord, so that he might be with his Lord in glory in the kingdom on high.

Whenever the evil injustice of the wicked assails us, let us call upon this man to rescue us from evildoers. Anyone who is oppressed and takes refuge in him with love and hope will no longer be defeated by the evildoers who wrong him. Anyone persecuted by the devil, the enemy of humanity, should take refuge in him, and the devil will flee from him like smoke. During his earthly life he drove away the tyrannical demons, and now, in his death, they tremble still more at the might of his power. During his earthly life they could not look at him, and now, in his death, they cannot even enter his dwelling. And if they do enter, they enter fearfully yet brazenly, proclaiming together their fear and their guilt. The rebels are truly filled with trembling and fear whenever they see the righteous man’s dwelling, even from far away. Whenever they see the righteous man’s monastery, it stands in their minds as a strong city that cannot be conquered by an adversary. They stand far away on the mountaintops and gaze at it, because they cannot approach its walls. Power comes forth from the treasured remains of the righteous man’s bones, and they see him as an army commander and flee from him. Come, let us be diligent on the day commemorating the glorious martyr, so that he may help us and we may not be harmed by the rebels. Come, let us be diligent in prayer on his feast day, so that we may be with him in the kingdom on high, amid the promised blessings.
On the Greek Fathers and Teachers

Discourse 10. On the Greek Fathers and Teachers. Again by the same author, this being his tenth discourse. Which concerns the fathers, the Greek teachers. Response. Give thanks to him who revealed the treasure of his wisdom to the friends he chose for himself. My brothers.

Righteous zeal on behalf of the righteous has greatly troubled me: why is the benefit of their labors denied? I saw the fruits of their work trampled among earthly people, and I grieved greatly at how, and how much, the righteous are wronged. The insolent inflicted a great injustice on those who know the truth, and [?] mocked and ridiculed their words. In their words humanity saw the truth clearly revealed, but the unfaithful turned dark before the light of faith. They purified the world with their insights as with salt, but the dull-hearted lost the taste of the life-giving word. They opened a path of life in creation for mortal humanity, but those dead in wickedness were not raised from their sins. The contentious became haters of life through their contentiousness, because they hated the word of truth spoken by those who possess knowledge. The truthful loved the word of truth above everything, but the haters of truth called them children of error. The force of their sayings openly proclaims the truth,

but fools cry out that the expression of their thoughts is false. Truth cries out like a trumpet within their books, but the ear of fools has become like a rock that cannot be softened. The truthful attended to the purpose of the divine Scriptures and carefully explained the force of their meanings. The rebel, the hater of humanity, saw the truth in them and stirred people up to hate them as though they were wicked. The evil zealot deceitfully planted a scheme in the minds of fools, so that they would revile the word of truth spoken by the wise. This teaching that has sprouted on earth is his own seed: it makes knowledgeable people hateful in the eyes of fools. Through the mouths of the ignorant he spews his gall against the wise, knowing that the meditation of their hearts is eager to drink in his words. The deceitful one habitually triumphs through deceitful people, and through them he shoots the arrows of his schemes into the ranks of the righteous. Through their mouths he fights against the truthful in every generation, and through their tongues he lays waste the ranks of faith. This has been his aim since the beginning of humanity's formation: to draw up a battle line against human beings by means of human beings. He habitually fights bodily against those who have bodies, since his own nature is uncompounded and invisible. Through the bodily serpent he first fought with speech, and through its tongue he sowed error in Eve's ears. With a hand of flesh he killed Abel, the firstborn of the righteous, and through envy he accomplished the desire of his own envy. Through an insolent mouth he reviled the righteous man who was free from wrongdoing, and the contemptible son mocked and laughed at his father. Through the brothers' envy, [?] he sold Joseph and made him a slave to the offspring of Canaan, the slave of slaves. Through an Israelite he drove Moses out of Pharaoh's household, and Moses hired himself out to a diviner, a priest of demons. Through Saul, a demon, a dwelling place of demons, he persecuted David, who suffered and groaned while living among foreigners. The deceitful one harmed all the righteous through his deceit, and there was no chaste person whom he did not mock through insolent mouths. His will is astonishing in the mouths of the insolent in every generation, and he has never stopped or neglected his battle against the truthful. Only with one human being did he halt his battling struggle, and after a time he returned to the warfare that is his trade. He loves to wage an unjust war against earth's inhabitants, and now he devises cunning schemes to fulfill his desire. He habitually battles against the truthful, entirely [?], and through liars he displays the power of his craft. Through the mouths of deceivers the fraudulent one expounds his fraud, and through their tongues he unleashes mockery against the chaste and the righteous. He has set his aim against the righteous to fight them, knowing that they can tear down the towering structure of his falsehood. The faithful tore down his falsehood with the power of their words, and for this reason he constantly barks at their pronouncements. Like a dog, his impulse barks through the mouths of the insolent.

He harasses the hearing of the wise with his persistence. The doglike one, the speaking dog, has acquired the habits of dogs; whenever he sees someone who will not listen to him, he grows unruly and inflamed. Now too he saw three men walking rightly, and he began to howl as he did at that time before our Lord. The righteous pricked him with a goad like that of the apostles, and he trembled and was terrified by the severity of their pronouncements. The workers of faith shot three arrows at him and taught him the power of the divinity hidden in a human being. In faith they made known the mystery of faith, revealing and displaying it to those in heaven and those on earth. The divine Being who became human placed a human being before humanity, so that people might be inclined to call him Word and body. Men of keen understanding proclaimed Word and body, and now savage demons and foolish people are raging. The righteous expounded one Being who is three, and joined one human being to that Being in unity. The faithful called the Word and the body by one name: Son of the divine Being and Son of humanity, one person. One is the Word, the Father's offspring without beginning, and one is the human son from the humanity of Adam. All that belongs to the divine Being and to the human being is two in nature; the Son of God is one in honor and authority. The Son of God is one person, not one in nature, for the divine Being is divine Being and the human being is human being: two who became one. This is the message that the righteous proclaimed in people's ears. Foolish people heard it and recoiled from understanding it. The three faithful men whom I mentioned directed themselves toward this goal, and they did not falter at the sound of mockery from demons and people. Demons and people reviled them as they would the evil one, because of the message of faith proclaimed on earth. They put on faith like a shield against every voice, and the arrows of insults did not pierce their limbs. Though bodily beings, they armed themselves spiritually, and in their bodies they overcame the sting of the passions. The struggle of their victories is full of great wonder: though mortal, they performed deeds that were not mortal. They were mortals, from the stock fashioned out of dust, and this is the wonder: in their very nature they conquered their nature. They exhausted the spring of passions flowing through their limbs, and their hearts poured forth a pure discourse of pure truth. A pure discourse sprang from people whose souls were pure, but evil demons and foolish people muddied its waters. Evil gall crushed those who hated their own souls, and they refused to receive the sweet drink of faith. Through faith the soul sees faith, and faith teaches it to see a vision that cannot be seen. The truthful proclaimed hidden things in their revelations and displayed them to the eyes of those watching as though in the light. The mystery of the one person, who is the self-existent one and a human being, was hidden and concealed from minds without understanding. The mystery that I said was hidden was hidden from those without understanding, because they do not know how to look carefully at things that are not revealed. To those with understanding, everything hidden and revealed is plain.

And they clearly disclose the mystery of hidden things. They clearly displayed the mystery of faith and set it up like an image on the earth before those watching. Human beings showed humanity a wondrous vision, but those who were not human did not contemplate its glory. The message he proclaimed among the inhabitants of earth was very glorious, and people who loved truth listened to it in a glorious way. Only fools refused to accept the persuasion offered concerning it, and they did not look carefully at the glory of its splendid beauty. Blind envy blinded those whose souls were blind, and they did not see the light that shines brighter than all lights. The light of the sun, however bright it may be, is nothing when compared with the radiance of the word of truth. The word of truth drove away the error of the darkness of the two, yet evil people help it return to inhabited places. The righteous drove the worship of demons out into the wilderness, so that human habitation would not be disturbed by its strife. Our dwelling was embattled, and the conduct of our lives was disturbed, until the one who orders everything brought peace through one human being. The power that fashioned humanity chose one from among human beings and placed power in him to reconcile everyone with everything. The one who orders everything chose him from among all for the peace of humanity, and nothing remained that he did not reconcile through him with his majesty. The one who establishes created things revealed the power of his majesty in our nature, and in his glory he honored our race, fashioned from dust. Lowly dust forgot its own nature and the one who gave it being, and began barking like a dog at the Lord who fashioned it. The wicked people of our day bark at the Lord who fashioned us through the insults their mouths spew against the truthful. Through the truthful, the one who desires our life revealed his will, and through them we gain the wisdom to know the mystery of his hidden things. He placed the treasury of his love in the hands of those who love love, so that they might lovingly distribute it to meet our need. Our race was needy and deprived of every good thing, and he placed his will in our fellow human beings so that they might nourish us. According to his will, the righteous sustained us in our poverty, and without begrudging anything they provided our lives with spiritual things. In a spiritual way they displayed the power of spiritual things, and through visible things they depicted for us a likeness of hidden things. The mystery of the revelation of the Son and the Spirit was hidden from us, and we did not know that they exist without beginning. The righteous enlightened us in our ignorance about things not revealed, and they taught us to invoke the three names in order. The idle people of our day have confused this order and have wronged the labors of those who established it through their efforts. The diligent undertook exhausting labors for this order, but deceitful workers called them lazy. Deceitful workers called those who worked well liars. Who would not grieve over this outrage, which is terrible even to hear? I was greatly astonished at this outrage, and I am still astonished. Because of it I have traveled far along the road of words. I saw that the teaching of the righteous was being wronged by oppressors, and I sought to know the reason for this injustice.

I chose three men from the entire company of the righteous, so that through their case I might reveal the case of them all. Oppressors have wronged the righteous in [?] generations, but more than all the others, they have grievously wronged those whom I mentioned. Those devoted to controversy reviled them beyond measure. Perhaps they learned this manner of abuse from demons. Demons cast foolish zeal into foolish people, so that they would revile the word of truth with a tongue of flesh. Demons are accustomed to blaspheme with a tongue of flesh, and behind fleshly people they conceal the deceit of their blasphemies. I saw that their blasphemies were utterly abhorrent and contemptible, and I was deeply stirred to demand an account from them for the dishonor done to the righteous. On behalf of the learned, I contend with the uneducated, who have become the devil’s companions in the conflict they are waging. It is a great battle in which people array themselves against other people, yet no one asks what the reason for this conflict is. All ranks have sunk into something like sleep over this matter. Now I seek to awaken them so that they may examine it. From now on I will openly explain the subject of my words, so that those who listen to these words may understand their meaning. I said [?] that foolish people had wronged righteous people. It is fitting that I reveal who has been wronged and who is the oppressor. Those who served well as priests have been wronged without cause: one is Diodore, another Theodore, and another Nestorius. These are the wronged men of whom I spoke at the beginning, and their oppressors are demons and heretical people. The heretics saw that their falsehoods had been exposed, and the men clothed in truth put on armor. Those clothed in truth demolished the error of those who had gone astray, and Diodore was more energetic in battle than anyone else. He fought against the factions of the heretics and exposed and revealed their deceit before everyone. With the sword of his word he destroyed the words of the deceitful, and they could not stand against the force of the words of his mouth. There were wolves whom he scattered with the sound of his proclamations, and he gathered the flock that had been scattered by their disputes. In the city of Antioch he began the battle against those who had gone astray. And after a time he completed his victory in the region of Tarsus. In the city of Tarsus the lot fell to him to serve as priest, where that herald of all the nations was born. In this city the teaching of the radiant priest triumphed, and there he was crowned like the victors who were not defeated but brought others low. The Lord of victors strengthened the valiant warriors, and he made them light and salt for the benefit of humanity. He sent Theodore to a city sick with sin, which was called by the worthless name of the demon Mopsus. The demon set up an idol in his own name and called it Mopsus, and that city too was called Mopsuestia. From one city came three lamps of light, and the light of their way of life shone in three cities.

All three were born in one city, and when they had grown up, they began the struggle for truth. Truth armed them with its strength like warriors and sent them to wage war against Satan. Love cast lots of love for all three of them, and each went out to the region that the divine command assigned him. The hidden divine command was concealed in Theodore’s words, and he interpreted hidden mysteries for the Mopsuestians. The inhabitants of Mopsuestia were called Mopsuestians after that demon in whose name a mute idol had been set up. The man of keen understanding wiped the hateful names away from them and made them pure vessels for the Creator’s name. In the Creator’s name the righteous man bound the city’s demon and taught it to repeat: three names, one Being. The warrior of righteousness held the three names and hurled them like arrows at the heretics. His voice was terrifying when he cried out against their divisions, and the insolent could not bear to listen to the meaning of his words. The embattled demons were astonished at the meaning of his words: “What is this? Though he is a human being, his voice makes us tremble!” The Creator performed a great wonder through the members of his household, and demons and human beings were defeated by the sound of their utterances. Demons and human beings heard the ringing sound of his trumpet-like voice, and they gathered, came, and drew up their battle lines against his words. A spring of spiritual words gushed from his mouth, and like a flood it swept away the army of the heretics. The Arians and Eunomians floated like driftwood, and with them the Dimoerites and the Apollinarians [?] perished. He scattered the divided factions like chaff, and they fled and hid among the cavities of their hiding places. The companies of those devoted to error fled in frantic flight before the man who expounded the pure truth. The liars heard the pure truth from the truthful, and they trembled and were terrified like a woman in labor overcome by pain. The power of miraculous signs exposed them as feeble warriors, and they threw down the weapons of their teachings and fled naked. Oh, how fearsome was the power that strengthened the warrior of the Spirit! At his voice the embattled throngs that the demons had assembled were defeated. Oh, how fearsome was the meaning of the words of his refutations! He exposed the various tricks of every teaching. Oh, how skillful was the mind of the upright man, more skillful than all others! He left nothing hidden without uncovering it and making it known. Oh, how discerning he was in searching the divine Scriptures! He explained the utterances of the prophets and the apostles. Oh, how swiftly the impulses of his soul ran together with his limbs! He encompassed the course of all the Scriptures within his words. Oh, that soul, skillful in understanding and mighty in strength, which prevailed and won both contests, against demons and against human beings!

The champion of righteousness defeated demons and human beings, and he did not falter in any struggle with any fierce opponent. He established an upright goal in the world for those who fight, so that they might incline toward reverence for the truth, following his example. His sayings became salt and light among the inhabitants of earth, and people learned to cleanse the garments of humanity. Humanity acquired a good flavor through his insights, and despised and cast away the perversity of demon worship. This man, mighty in strength and skillful in understanding, was hated by people who hated their own souls and were full of pride. The word of truth appointed him to be a herald of truth, but fools called him divided in mind and a teacher of falsehood. Oh, those perverse people! How perverse, how perverse was their perversity! They called the radiant man darkness, and darkness light. The unjust deserve the woe pronounced by the prophetic word, for they overturned the order of things rightly established, turning them into their opposites. The perverse, who hated their own souls, loved perverse things, and detested and hated people who loved the faith. The righteous men Diodorus and Theodore, together with Nestorius, proclaimed the faith that cannot be defeated. Through the three of them the Trinity displayed its power and taught them to refute the fabrications of erroneous teaching. It appointed them as chosen priests in three cities, so that they might heal severe afflictions with their sayings. They were true healers of humanity wherever they were, and they carefully shepherded the flock of rational sheep. These diligent men listened to the voice that spoke to Simon, and they made disciples and taught men, women, and children. Through their deeds they fully lived up to the title of shepherd, and each of them cared for his flock without neglect. Diodorus, skilled in disputation, shepherded the people of Tarsus. He taught them how to untie the knots of the heretics. Theodore, the revealer of mysteries, shepherded the people of Mopsuestia and taught them to examine carefully things that are not revealed. Nestorius, keen in his activity, shepherded the people of Byzantium and taught them how to engage in the contest against heresies. The imperial city fell to the upright man to govern, and in keeping with his rank he displayed the fruits of his teaching. He wisely built up the firm foundation of the word of truth, so that the turbulent blasts of the heretics would not shake it. The heretics hated the lover of truth without cause and devised deceitful schemes against his words. Fraudulent smiths forged cunning schemes to bind words that cannot be grasped by the hand of deceit. The insolent acted deceitfully against the truthful, and without cause they fabricated a false accusation. Liars chose false witnesses for the trial of the righteous man, following the same pattern that Jezebel used in Naboth’s trial. A woman killed righteous Naboth because of his vineyard, and women persecuted the truthful man and drove him from his priesthood. Women hired false priests for a fraudulent trial,

and made them advocates of falsehood. For gold they sold pure truth, which cannot be sold, and between buyer and seller they wronged the righteous. Mute silver drove the righteous man out of peace, and although it was utterly mute, it raised its voice against justice. Oh, how justice was silenced in her demands! She did not rebuke blatant deceit as she usually does. Oh, how great was the injustice that priests inflicted on priests! They neither trembled nor feared before the priesthood [?] in which they ministered. Come now, priests, and see what a hundred [?] priests did: they unjustly drove a priest from the priesthood. Insolently they drove the righteous man from his priesthood, and unjustly they passed sentence and cast him into exile. If anyone says that I have spoken these things unjustly, let him demonstrate it openly, and I will pay the penalty for my words. Come, show me, you who judge against my words: what are the grounds for this man’s condemnation? Reveal and explain clearly to me the nature of his offense, and I will agree with you that you rightly condemned the offender. I said these things to those who revile him, and I say them again: let them show us the nature of the offense for which he was condemned. Indeed, no one can speak against my words, because he does not know how to follow the path of answering an argument. You do not know how to put together a persuasive argument. If you wish, listen to me, and I will tell you what you do not know. I will explain the cause of this conflict and where the slander against this man originated. The evil envy of evil men hated the upright man because of the faith that he expounded well. The leader of Egypt was sick and weak in this matter, and when he heard a voice cutting into his ailment, he grew jealous and furious. The Egyptian saw the incision made by the skilled healer’s word, and he was displeased with the teaching that was full of every kind of healing. “Why,” he said, “does he proclaim two names, ‘Word’ and ‘body’? And why does he use the word ‘form’ of both the servant and the Maker?” “Why does he not say that Mary is the mother [?] of the divinity, that she gave birth bodily to the One who exists, since he became flesh?” This was the reason for the Egyptian’s envy, and because of this he hated the upright man as though he were evil. Envy inflamed the envious man against the righteous man because it had fallen to him to govern the city of kings. Envy forged instruments of deceit in its cunning and put them into human hands to overthrow the truth. It gathered an assembly of impostors and brought them against the truthful man, calling them a chosen and pure synod. This assembly drove the priest from his priesthood, with the cooperation of women, and aided the folly of the priests. This was the charge on which the innocent man was condemned, and news of his condemnation spread falsely.

Deceitful men hid treacherous snares for the man pure in soul. Without cause they reviled him as an enemy of the faith. Now I have shown the reason for the trial of the wronged man, whom deceitful men unjustly condemned. Now I have also exposed the envy of the envious man, who wronged the noble priest without cause through disgraceful deeds. It was not just for the priest to leave his priesthood, nor was it right for deceitful men to acquire his rank. Look, people, how many things rightly ordered the envious have overturned! Look and consider how evil envy is! Now the deceptive disguise of the deceivers has been exposed: they unjustly claimed justice in the judgment they pronounced. If anyone says that I have not recounted the matter fairly, let him tell me where I departed from what was right. What have I said that I did not state as it actually was? Let anyone who has a clear statement to make show it openly. You have no man who can answer my words with contrary arguments or show that the judgment condemning the righteous man was just. And suppose someone says, ‘Here I am, a priest [?].’ They pronounced the sentence. Why do they condemn those who are not guilty as though they were guilty? Look, Diodore and Theodore are righteous men. No one can say that a human court condemned them. Why do the dull-hearted revile the learned, and why do they flee from the wisdom of their interpretations? No inquiry into their words arose until evil envy sprang up among evil men. In their days there was no synodal assembly, nor any command gathering priests to investigate accusations. There were three assemblies in the land of the Romans. The time of each is known, and its occasion is clear. One assembled in the days of Emperor Constantine because of the wickedness that suddenly sprang from the mouth of Arius. The second took place in the days of Theodosius because of the vile invention that Macedonius brought forth. The third took place under the rule of two emperors, and its occasion was the envy of the Egyptian. These, then, are the three synods that took place at three different times. At none of them were the three men I mentioned present. At the first, Diodore and his companions had not yet been born. Who could conduct a trial against people not yet born? At the second, they had not yet attained leadership. It is therefore clear that the assemblies did not summon them for judgment. At the third [?], they had departed from among the living. Who would be so mad as to accuse the dead without cause? Look, the cause that provokes these kinds of insults has been revealed. Let us therefore investigate why the righteous are insulted. Why do troubled people fight against upright people, and why do those who hate their own souls speak mockingly about good people? Why do they declare that the books they wrote are untrue, when even the rising sun is not as clear as their words? Why do they call the words of the synodical anathema false?

For no council has accused them of anything shameful. And if they mention that ecumenical council, what connection did it have with people who were already dead? And if they pursue the case of Nestorius at that time, look: he himself did not even hear the proceedings that determined his sentence. He was not present before the judges who condemned him without cause, since he had withdrawn before coming before his judges. Who has ever heard of anything like what the priests did: passing sentence when the defendant was not present? The judges conducted this trial with partiality, and out of deference to a person they were ashamed to make the truth openly known. The wise and intelligent deferred to the Egyptian, and fear of [?] frightened them away from speaking the truth. And indeed, they understood the intention of the Egyptian's words, but they did not agree with the anathemas that they had written in an accursed manner. In an accursed manner they pronounced anathemas against those who knew the truth, and their accursed conduct was not hidden from their eyes. Look, they themselves also anathematized the anathemas he had invented. Nor did they anathematize only his anathemas: they included him too under the anathema. For this is what is written in the document of their faith: “Anyone who uses the term ‘mixture’ is anathematized.” Yet the Egyptian established an anathema contrary to this: no one is permitted to say “body and divinity.” What, then, is someone who hears these things to do, when both the person who confesses correctly and the person who does not confess are anathematized? See what partiality did to intelligent people: they judged justly, and then turned around and condemned unjustly. The anathema that overturned the Egyptian's words was just, but it was not just to destroy the man who refuted them. Envy brought about a great disaster concerning his anathemas: they lumped together the one who annulled anathemas and the one who imposed anathemas. The ecumenical council mixed anathema with anathema, and they stirred up strife between the knowledgeable and the ignorant. No one can separate one anathema from its opposite, since both anathemas are included under a single anathema. This confusion has disturbed the world with its disorder. Now love is divided, and there is no harmony between one person and another. There is no harmony at all among the inhabitants of the earth, especially among the people whom Christ chose for his name. Among Christians, divisions have multiplied beyond counting, and no one knows how to walk rightly on the path of truth. I saw the path of truth deserted by travelers, and I marveled greatly at what the wickedness of women had done. I saw that the wickedness of women had thrown human life into confusion, and I told myself that I had not acted justly in looking on and remaining silent. I judged myself in matters that a rational being can judge: why had I neglected the accusations that could be made in words? It is very easy for one endowed with speech to restrain injustice, and it is a simple thing for him to silence the various forms of evil.

I saw that various forms of evil were widespread among those on earth, and my mind advised me to pronounce judgment in righteous words. I have a case to argue in words with those endowed with speech: why do they refrain from words that judge other words? I heard foolish people uttering unjust speech, and I composed words to oppose their improper words. I saw righteous people being wronged by ignorant people, and I was not pleased to hear the [?] of fools. I read the books they wrote and reflected on how distinguished they were. I marveled greatly at how grievously they were wronged by oppressors. I wanted to accuse their oppressors with the sound of my words: why do they wrong those who are not lacking in righteousness? Why, oppressors, have you so grievously wronged those pure in soul and rejected the good teaching found in their words? What wrong have the righteous committed, when they have done no wrong? Yet they are persecuted for their words as though they were evildoers. If it is wrong for someone to meditate on the faith, then all the righteous have spent their lives in this meditation. And if it is a crime to speak the truth [?] concealment, then the apostolic preachers themselves laid out this path. Indeed, the head of the Twelve cried out to the Jews that Jesus is a man, a human being from God. Paul too, distinguished among the apostles, agrees with this and calls him the one mediator between the Eternal One and us. Luke and Matthew wrote his history without concealment and listed his ancestors one after another. The Son of Thunder too revealed his humanity in plain speech: when it is dissolved, divine power raises it up. Let anyone who finds fault, then, find fault with those preachers themselves, for the distinction between the Word and the body is written in their books.
