And when he wishes to prophesy about his death, he foretells what he will do at the time of his suffering. The coming king makes his clothing white in pure wine, and in the blood of grapes the covering in which he wraps himself.

The blessing you pronounce is hidden, righteous Jacob! How can garments become white in wine, which stains clothes? And if his covering is something made, which everyone can see, perhaps its wearer is greater than the kings who preceded him. The words you spoke in the form of a blessing are not clear to everyone, nor does everyone know how the garments you mentioned become white. No, Jacob’s saying is not hidden from those with discernment, and it is a great strength for the faith of the orthodox. The wine is death, by which the human race is stained; but ravenous death does not stain the body he put on. And because he humbled himself and surrendered himself to the suffering of death, he ascended to heaven and was deemed worthy of a seat at the right hand. He makes white in wine the garment he put on from our humanity, and in the blood of grapes that covering from the house of David. What he said prophetically about his death is a crushing blow against Cyril, the apostle of falsehood. What will that man who attributes suffering to the Godhead say against Jacob, who handed over to death the body taken from us? In the creed that [?] composed there is an anathema, and he placed Jacob at the head of the anathema, so that they might make Jacob suffer. Do not be distressed by Cyril, King Jacob! Along with you, he anathematized everyone who says that Christ died. The misguided man anathematized the Holy Spirit and the apostles, and in his recklessness he even included our Lord himself in the anathema. Let the misguided man hear: which garment does wine make white—the one from Mary, or the one woven by hands? If you say that Jacob was speaking of the clothing he wore, clothes never become white in wine according to your interpretation.

Wine stains a vessel when it reaches it. Of which one, then, did Jacob say that it makes it white? You do not agree that this concerns the body he took from us. To what, then, does your mind incline in interpreting it? For I know that, as your audacity habitually does, your mind hands the Only Begotten over to suffering. O interpretation entirely filled with audacity! O blasphemy that justice will not pardon! Far be it from us to say this, that God suffered! Let us not join the faction that subjected the Only Begotten to suffering. Let our assembly rejoice, for Zechariah the prophet gives it joy. Let the Church exult in place of the daughter of Zion, who is [?]. The prophet brought the daughter of Jerusalem the good news, “Your king is coming,” so that when she saw him she would go out to meet him and welcome him. “Exult and rejoice, daughter of Jerusalem!” the herald cried. “Look, your glorious king is coming to you and bringing you joy!” The daughter of Jerusalem did not ask him what his identifying sign was, yet he began explaining his way of acting to her, as he had been commanded. “Your king is humbler than all kings by his own choice. He rides a colt, yet his command rules over the heights and the depths. “Throw off the burden of sorrows that surround you, and do not lose heart because of the multitude of nations encircling you. “He is righteous,” he said, “and humble, and a savior. He also speaks peace with the nations, for they belong to him. “He will destroy the swift-running horse from Jerusalem, and he will also remove the chariot from Ephraim, so that it will be no more.” O messenger who brought good news to his own people, who made them rejoice and made them grieve through his proclamation! For by saying, “Your king is coming,” he made them rejoice.

But when he showed them his way of acting, he saddened them. They did not rejoice when he prophesied that he would ride a colt, for they thought that a colt could not wage war. And when he announced that he would destroy the horse and the chariot, they thought, “Our precious possessions have been taken away from us.” And because he proclaimed that he would also speak peace with the nations, they understood that perhaps the nations had become members of the household. Zion, the lover of pride, stood amid doubts, for she [?] the sign of the king whom the prophet proclaimed through the Spirit. “How can I rejoice at this news?” Jerusalem answered, for the horse and the chariot would disappear from her streets. “What can the lover of pride exult in, O herald, when the mount of the king you announced is a donkey’s colt? “Let the nations rejoice at this good news you announce, for he speaks peace and concord with them, as you prophesied.” “If you want him to speak peace and concord with you, look, you have heard his identifying sign, so that when you see him you may go out to meet him. “Had you not learned beforehand about his appearance, perhaps you would have had room for an excuse when he calls you to account.” The words the prophet spoke through the Spirit were fulfilled in deed, and Zion saw her king coming but did not receive him. He rode on a colt, the foal of a donkey, and entered Jerusalem, so that the word the prophet proclaimed through the Spirit would not prove false. His power stirred the great crowds that thirsted for blood, and they went out to meet him with olive branches to praise him. Not every time our Lord entered Jerusalem did they go out to meet him as they went out on this day. On this day great crowds went out to meet him,

to see his glory and Lazarus, whom his command had brought to life. They did not understand why they were going out, for a hidden power stirred them to go out to meet him. One carried olive branches and offered praise; another spread his clothes on the road where he was passing. There were women singing before him with lyres, and the sound of the hosannas in their songs shook Zion. The Pharisees and scribes closed their mouths against praising him, and nursing infants praised him in their place. The praise of nursing infants surpassed that of their fathers, for they cried out a new praise that no one had heard. Beyond the power of nature, nursing infants spoke a new utterance with which no human tongue had offered praise. The infants sang a new praise to the new king with new mouths from which no other word had come. “Let there be hosanna in the heights!” the children cried, “and hosanna also to the Son of David, who is glory!” A great wonder took place in Jerusalem on this day, but the unruly Jewish people did not understand. For one wonder was that her king rode on the foal of a donkey—he whose divine glory the cherubim escort in procession. Another wonder was that the crowds went out with olive branches, without knowing why their ranks had gone out. They knew only to go out in great numbers; they did not know what to say as they went out. Another wonder, at which heaven and earth marveled, was that nursing children cried out, “Hosanna!” The infants rebuked the scribes and priests with their hosannas,

and with tongues they had never used for speech, they spoke new things. In their jealousy, the scribes and priests could not bear the new praise proclaimed by the mouths of nursing infants. The wrongdoers heard the sound of praise spoken by the infants, and jealousy against our Savior grew fierce in their hearts. They saw young men and young women singing praise, and they began to groan like a woman in labor overcome by pain. The infants and crowds cried out, “Blessed is our God!” But they burned with anger against our Savior: “Rebuke your disciples!” “Are they blind, blind at heart?” our Savior exclaimed. “They are your children, who do not believe in me through their bodily senses. For they have not yet heard the sound of my proclamation with their ears, nor have their eyes seen the signs my hands have performed. You have seen the dead whom I raised from their graves, and you even threatened death against the dead man whom my will brought to life. You have heard the words of prophecy spoken by righteous Jacob, King David, and Zechariah as well. Jacob blessed his offspring and gave him good news about me: that prophets and kings would come from him until my coming. He gave a sign that I would be carried in procession on the back of a colt. And look, it has been fulfilled this very day, yet you have not believed. And the sign that Jacob gave in the [?] of the blessing, Zechariah also gave, so that when you saw me you would not doubt. David also revealed through the Holy Spirit the matter of the children who offered praise contrary to their usual practice, so that you might be further assured. ‘From the mouths of young men and newborn children,’ he said, ‘he established the praise they sing to the Lord, our Lord.’ David had already foreseen in the Spirit your vengeance against me:

He explained and said that the children offered praise because of you. Perhaps you will say in your pride-loving minds, ‘Poverty made him ride a lowly colt.’ It was not because I lacked a swift-running mount that I rode a slow-moving colt before your crowds. For heaven and earth and everything in them are mine, and my will rules over the animals and the birds. The donkey’s colt did not belong to the man who sent it to me. The power of my lordship moved him, and he did not resist. Just as I moved the man who owned the donkey’s colt, I could also have moved someone who owned a herd of horses. What I did today in riding a colt was so that what the prophets prophesied through the Spirit might be fulfilled in me. For this is one purpose: that I should bring our prophecy to completion and give my servants an example of humility. For if I, who am the Lord, rode a colt, how much more should they refrain from being carried in procession in carriages! All the kings who were carried in procession in carriages did not bring peace to the earth through their mounts. But I, who chose to ride a colt in my humility—through me heaven and earth are brought to peace and are not shaken. Why do you tell me to rebuke the children who praise me? Silence them yourselves; perhaps your words will silence them. And if you are annoyed by the sound of the hosannas with which they praise me, teach them, so that perhaps they will be silent as you are. And if you tell me to rebuke the children who sing praise, the stones will cry out another praise greater than this. And if the stones sing praise to the God of all:

You priests of daughter Jerusalem, whom do you envy? Our Savior did all these things on this day, as his prophets foretold through the Spirit who taught them. The crowds went out to meet our Lord with olive branches. Let us also drive envy out of ourselves, for it is the offspring of the evil one. May baptism, the spiritual mother, no longer bear a child who carries out the evil desire of the accuser. Let whoever drinks the precious blood that the spear pressed out live out his life according to the will of our Lord Jesus [?]. Let whoever runs the noble race of righteousness cause error to flee from the sound of his voice wherever he preaches. Let whoever has been chosen to serve as a priest in the holy Church shepherd his flock according to the will of the high priest. Let everyone entrusted with resources [?] in this world use them to satisfy anyone who needs food. So that on that day when the King on high comes in his glory, we may be worthy to enter the kingdom he promised us.
For Palm Sunday.

Discourse 21. For Palm Sunday. By the same author: the twenty-first discourse, suitable for Palm Sunday. Response: Son who was praised by the mouths of children, strengthen ours, so that we may welcome you with hosannas. My brothers.

The glorious radiance from the Father, the Son who is not younger than the one who begot him, the eternal [?] Word of the Father, who has been with his Father from eternity [?]. He rose like the sun in our humanity and filled the world with his glory. He drove away and extinguished the darkness through the rays of his splendor. Since the eye could not see him or gaze upon his nature, he concealed the radiance of his majesty in the firstfruits he put on from us. He showed created beings his glory, not his hidden nature. He made known to us the power of his lordship, not the limits of his being. In his love, the Word of the Father put on the garment of our body and dwelt in it. Through it he explained to rational beings the power revealed in his wisdom. His love fashioned a silent harp of flesh for his revelation, so that through its songs he might gladden spiritual and bodily beings. His hidden will played upon the strings of a mortal body, and human beings and angels marveled at the sweetness of his melodies. [?] the image of his being, he honored it above everything through his love. Through it he gladdened creation when it had been embittered by sins. Through human wrongdoing, the peace of the whole inhabited world was disturbed. His glory dwelt in a human being so that through him he might bring peace to creation. The hidden, wondrous mystery came into the open through his mercy: the one whom heavenly and earthly beings longed to see. By his coming he confirmed the Scriptures, which taught us that he was to come. He fulfilled and completed the words of the prophets who proclaimed his mysteries. What he promised came to pass [?], and he was revealed from the offspring of David. As was spoken ages ago through the mouths of all his holy ones. By his birth he freed us from error and sanctified us through the mysteries of his baptism. He set before us a pattern of purity through his radiant and holy fast. And when he saw how greatly the demons had exalted themselves in pride over our race, he chose, in the form of our lowliness, to put an end to the rebel’s pride. For he rode on a lowly colt and entered the city of Jerusalem. Young people, children, and infants took branches in their hands, crying out, “Hosanna to the king who has arisen from David!” For on this day the saying of righteous Jacob was fulfilled, which he had prophesied beforehand about his coming to us: “The scepter that ruled over Judah shall not depart, nor the revealer of hidden things and the prophet from between his feet, until he comes to whom royal authority belongs.” Then, he says, king and prophet shall cease from Judah. His is the eternal kingdom, without end, through all generations. He is the fulfillment of the mysteries and the hope of all the nations.

Just as Jacob prophesied, as he learned through revelation, in accordance with his saying there is neither king nor prophet in Judah. Judah cannot say that he has a king from his own race, nor can he show that he has a prophet [?]. If prophet and king have now departed from him, as indeed they have departed, then the prophecy of our father Jacob has reached its fulfillment in this one. Do not waver in your thoughts, son of Abraham [?], marked by circumcision. Consider discerningly the words of righteous Jacob. Look at the signs he gave beforehand and set out for you concerning the one who is coming, who was to come and bring an end to prophets and kings among your people. For he said that he would tie his colt, the foal of his donkey, to a vine. And the colt, he says, would not become unruly and break a shoot from it. By this sign he showed us the power to which everything is subject. Like a colt, he subdues tyrants beneath his kingship. And on this day he rode on a colt and entered Jerusalem, so that the word spoken by the prophet through the Spirit generations before would not fail. Zechariah the prophet, son of Jacob, also made it known, like his father. He proclaimed him, speaking joyfully in his prophecy. He tightened the strings of his harp and raised his voice, saying: “Rejoice and be glad, daughter of Zion! Shout for joy, for your king has come! Look, your Savior has arrived, riding on a donkey’s colt. Open your gates to him, Jerusalem, for the Savior has come to you. Rejoice greatly, then, daughter of Zion, and cry out fitting praise to him. Accept his gentle yoke and worship him with a pure heart.” The daughter of Zion did not ask him, “What is the sign of that king?” And he began to explain to her through his words what he would do at his coming: “Your king is humbler than kings, and he has humbled himself willingly. He rides on a lowly colt, though he rules over the heights and the depths. Cast off all your burdens and the afflictions that surround you.” Do not grow faint with fear because of the nations that hate you. Your king is righteous and humble, and he is a savior. He speaks peace to the nations, for they too belong to him. He also said that he would destroy the swift horse from Jerusalem. He removes the chariot from Ephraim and abolishes it so that it will be no more. For Jerusalem, who loved wrongdoing, stood amid divisions. When she heard the sign of the king, which Zechariah proclaimed to her through the Spirit, the words announced about his coming were fulfilled in deed. He came to enter Jerusalem, but Zion’s children did not receive him. The elders therefore withheld the praise of the king who came to them, while the children were stirred by wonder to praise him with hosannas.

The young people paid him the praise that the elders of daughter Zion owed him. There the song of praise required for his honor was made ready. The unjust priests, scribes, and Pharisees had shut their mouths. The children stood in groups to acclaim him with hosannas. “Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord!” those of innocent soul cried out to him. The road of the King’s Son thundered as they acclaimed him with new praise. They [?] the trees to give him branches of olive and palm. So that his road, the road of the heavenly [?], might be adorned with their fruit. The children wove and offered crowns of praise with the branches of their tongues. They rejoiced in Christ, whom they saw among their gatherings. It was not every time our Lord entered Jerusalem that they went out to meet him as the children went out on this day to praise him. On this day [?], great crowds went out to meet him, to see the glory of his greatness in Lazarus, the dead man who had come to life. Yet they went out without understanding the reason for their going out. For his own power stirred them to go out to meet him with hosannas. Some carried olive branches, and others palm fronds. Others spread their garments on the road along which our Lord walked. There were also young people there who sang to the accompaniment of lyres. At the sound of their hosannas, the city of Zion was shaken. The Pharisees and scribes kept their mouths from praising our Savior, and little children acclaimed him in their place, in an indescribable marvel. The praise of nursing infants amazed their fathers, for they cried out a new song of praise that no one had ever heard before. The little children spoke beyond the powers of nature before Christ—a new utterance, the like of which no human tongue had spoken. The little children sang new praise to the new king descended from David, with fresh mouths from which not a word had yet come. “Hosanna in the highest!” the children cried aloud. “Hosanna also to the Son of David!” Its meaning is “praise.” Zechariah called out to daughter Zion to join the children in praise. The contemptuous bride did not heed the prophet’s delightful voice. For she was defiled by carved images; because of this, [?] she was distressed that he had come. And so she paid no heed [?] when she met her betrothed. For her heart was captivated by the calf, and she loved it shamefully. That is why she did not listen to the prophet who cried, “Rejoice!” For the daughter of Zion was entangled with the four-faced image. She would not open the door to Christ, who had come to her. She was intent on serving her idols with reverence. She cared nothing for her Lord’s glory, and she turned her face away from his radiance. She openly worshiped Ishtar and mourned for Tammuz. The deceitful woman loved Milcom and offered sacrifices to Baal.

She was constantly occupied with Egyptian songs, and she had no time to sing praise to the Son with the children. She was eager to prepare sacrifices for demons without delay. She did not go out to carry branches with the children amid their hosannas. The children [?] were blessing and praising the King who had humbled himself to come to her. But Zion was polishing an image and behaving foolishly with her idols. The prophets [?] knocked at her doors, rousing her from sleep. But she lay asleep in her sins, with the evil demons she loved. “Rejoice, daughter of Zion!” But she did not rejoice, for she loved calves and carved images. She was distressed that the pure Bridegroom was coming to her city. For she knew that he would expose her, and for this reason she hated him without cause. The unjust woman did not want him to be praised by the children. In envy she blinded her heart; she became deaf and ceased to offer praise. She was intent on silencing those who praised him, stopping their praise of him. She herself would not praise the King who had come to save her. She was eager to stop the praise that the children shouted to him. They were praising joyfully, but she was angered by their voices. She threatened them to make them fall silent, but the children shouted all the more. She wanted only for them to fall silent, and she was eager in her efforts. She sought ways to fulfill her desire, so that their hearts might be silenced. Those praising the Son of David would not stop their praise, for truth had stirred them to praise him with their voices. There was a marvel at his entrance, a wonder to those with discernment, which neither heavenly nor earthly beings could adequately describe. For the crowds rejoiced in its joy, and the children were glad in it. They danced before the King’s Son, as David had before the ark. The children [?] sang him a new song of praise befitting God, and sang to the Son of David, who in his love raised our lowliness through his [?]. With David his father, they cried out [?] to the Son of David with their hallelujahs. They sounded their trumpets with the songs of the heavenly watchers. With the loud sound of horns, with lyres and harps, with flutes and every kind of song, with the melodies of their music. With four-stringed instruments and resounding cymbals, sing on sweet strings to him who was exalted in his humility and conquered the rebel’s strongholds. With their branches in their hands and their hosannas in their mouths. With myrtles, olive branches, and every kind of tree, they proclaim the praise of his greatness. For it was their custom to honor their [?]. With palm fronds and citrons, they went out to meet him. He received praise from little children and songs of praise from their crowds. The angels thundered in heaven at the wonders of his entry. The watchers stood in great amazement on the day of our Savior’s entry. When they saw him riding on a colt and moving through the streets of the city. The heavenly beings looked and saw him, humble and quiet in his gentleness, among the crowds of mortals.

And they marveled at his humility. The angels were amazed at these things: that he was being praised in both realms. On high by their [?], and below by children and little ones. They were all gazing at his great throne in heaven, and they saw him clothed in a bodily robe, acclaimed with hosannas. He rides the highest heavens in his hidden nature; he rides a colt in his humanity. The authority of his divinity rules in the heights and in the depths. In heaven his lightning flashes are humbled, and the earth with garments and branches. As watchers [?] and human beings alike cry hosanna to him. Cherubim and seraphim tremble to [?] his name on high. But children and little ones proclaim his praise fearlessly in his depths. Yet when Daughter Zion saw him, she envied him as he was being praised. She wanted his praise to cease from every mouth and from everyone praising him. She agreed neither with those above nor with those below who were praising him. She watched our Savior’s path, which is full of wonder and amazement. For the crucifier labored hard to silence the children. But because their mouths were full of truth, their voices were not silenced. The chiefs of the angels praise the Son in his holy dwelling, while in the streets of Daughter Zion innocent voices cry hosannas. From the [?] of his praise, he was being praised by little children. They reproached him, saying, “Why have you seized praise that was not yours?” They rebuked the children so that they would stop praising him. They supposed that when the children fell silent, the praise of his glory would cease. O unjust Jews, haters of the true light! How can his praise cease, when heaven and earth are full of it? If, in your contentiousness, you let the disciples and the children go. Look, he has hosts on high who praise him without ceasing: myriads upon myriads of angels, and a thousand thousands of seraphim. Look, those surrounding his glorious throne proclaim him holy with their voices. So it is no great thing that he should be praised by earthly beings, for whose sake he put on a body to save them from death. Listen and marvel, you discerning people, at the insolence of those who crucified him: how they burned with envy and hated their Savior without cause. For those who hated their own souls listened and heard his praise from the crowds, the children, and the infants, and could not [?] endure it. With evil and bitter hearts they approached the one who brings peace to all. They said to him, “Rebuke the children, for it is not [?] that you should be praised like this.” Our Lord answered and said to them, “Have you never read what is written: ‘From the [?] of all infants the Lord’s praise has been established’?” Order requires that they [?], all [?] in it [?]. “And so, if these fall silent, these stones will cry out.” And it is indeed just as our Savior said. For if these crowds had fallen silent,

the stones would have proclaimed his praise. It was a time when it was fitting for the Son to be praised by all. If the infants had [?], the stones would have cried out his praise. If the children and infants had not praised him with palm branches, mute [?] would have praised him at the time of his entry. The Lord of kings humbled himself, and in his humility he rode a colt. The crowds were moved to give praise for his humiliation on our behalf. The leaders of the peoples in Jerusalem, together with the crowds, were bound to proclaim his praise when he came to them. And because the priests [?] his praise, which they were bound to offer, the children cried out praises to him, to the King’s Son, with their hosannas. And if those praising him had fallen silent, praise would not have ceased there. For the stones would have stirred and cried out to him, “Hosanna to the King of kings!” All creation marveled at the humility of his coming. It was stirred to give praise with a loud voice, with hosannas. For those who understand know that the word our Savior spoke is true: if he commanded, the rocks and stones would cry out praise of his majesty. He said this to anyone who needed proof of the truth, so that through visible things he could easily understand hidden things. At his crucifixion on the wood, those who praised him were silent. The stones and rocks cried out the praise they owed to his divinity, in place of the disciples and children who did not praise him as he hung on the wood. The dead came out of their tombs and shouted praise to his glory. None of the natures in [?] denies our Lord his praise. Look, they are stirred to praise his lordship at all times. Even through stones and pieces of wood, it is easy for his [?] to speak. At his command he [?] the created beings, which proclaim the greatness of his glory. Those that speak, together with those that are silent, are singing through their very forms. Praise befitting his honor is hidden within their natures. At the wonder that took place today, those who speak and those who are mute were amazed. Yet the unruly Jewish people did not understand his power. This is one wonder: our Lord is riding on a colt. He is the one whose glorious lordship the cherubim celebrate on high. And this is another wonder: they went out with branches to meet him. They did not know why they were honoring him in procession with their [?]. This is the third wonder, at which heaven and earth were amazed: nursing infants were crying out hosannas to him. The children rebuked the priests and the scribes with their hosannas. Although they had not yet learned to speak, they proclaimed new things with their voices. Today the crowds praised him with praises beyond words, the King who triumphed in battle against death and Satan. For today the heavenly spirits praised the Son together with the crowds, when they saw him humbling himself on a weak and lowly mount. And in place of Zion, who hated him

and did not cling to his love, now all the nations praise him in the holy Church, which has loved him. The nations that have turned to know him [?] at his holy feasts. They celebrate his coming in place of the wrongdoers who did not welcome him, as young men, old men, and children praise him with their [?]. With songs of the Holy Spirit they sing praise to his lordship. Consider this, then, you congregations redeemed by the cross, and learn the mystery of his truth, which he fulfilled for us today. For he rode on a colt not because he had no horses, but to give us an example, so that we might imitate his humility. A mirror of his virtues [?] before our eyes, so that we might see the faults in our conduct and not become puffed up with empty glory. For he has invited us to his kingdom by coming to us. Let us prepare our banquet clothes so that we may enter his bridal chamber with him. He requires clean clothes of us on the great day of his appearing. Let us clothe ourselves in purity of soul, and let us too honor him in procession with purity. With unceasing hallelujahs let us exalt his [?] name. Let us all cry out together: Hosanna to you in the highest! Hosanna to the Son of David! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord!
Against the Jews
This is recited at the Feast of Hosannas and is directed against the Jews. Response: Blessed is the Lord who chose praise for his honor from the mouths of children, my brothers.

Come, Jew, proud of bodily titles; reveal and explain to me the reason your people were chosen. Why were you chosen from among all for the God of all, and honored in name and rank above the nations? Why are you separated from the families of the whole world, and why do you not mingle with the nations descended from Adam? Why do you estrange yourself like a foreigner from those of your own race? For you too belong to the stock of humanity, fashioned from dust. The nature of Adam’s descendants is one, O son of Adam, and one is the power that formed Adam and his offspring. Nature testifies that there is one nature and one Creator. And if they are one, why the distinction between the people and the nations? If a single command created everything from nothing,

why do you divide the creation, made equal, by your inequality? If the power that created speaking and speechless creatures is just, why is its treatment of its creatures not equal? Why did he choose you from all the nations and reject the rest? And why did he make a promise to you and not to everyone? Why did he confine the flow of the spirit of his revelations to your people, and restrict and contain prophecy within your tribes? Why did he give you alone the life-giving law, and exclude the nations from the sweetness of its great spring? Why did he display the power of his signs and mighty deeds among you, chastise nations, and rebuke kings for your sake? Was your love for him perhaps more abundant than everyone else’s, and did he therefore repay you with a reward worthy of your love? Or perhaps his love honored Abram’s love, and therefore made you an heir to his great love? Then let us inquire why he chose Abraham, and what the reason was that he called him a friend of his goodness. If you say that his love made him a friend of the Hidden One, look: his election preceded his love, and Moses bears witness. The spirit of revelation called him from Babylon before he believed, and after he set him apart, he abandoned paganism and honored the truth. Then neither you nor your ancestors have grounds for boasting, for your election belongs to another, who chooses and rejects. And suppose it was Abram’s love that made him chosen: there were those who loved more than he did before his election. Abel loved and showed his love through action. His murder testifies to his love; envy killed him. Noah too was pleasing in a wicked generation that corrupted its way. The testimony to the purity of his soul is there in the book of Moses. Melchizedek too served as priest and was exalted before his God. Let Abram speak, who bowed his head before his blessings.

Look, son of Abraham: there were righteous men like your father. Why was the promise made to your father and not to them? Why did he promise him, “In you the nations of the earth will be blessed,” and not wish to fulfill the promise of his words, as you [?]? I said this according to your way of thinking. Even if you are unwilling, concede to me that it is true that this was fulfilled through deeds. Why did he change his former name and call him by another? And why did he give him fatherhood over all the nations? Abram is a father who rules over just one people, while the name Abraham signifies fatherhood over many. His former name did not contain faith, but once he was established in faith, he became Abraham. One Being revealed and explained the meaning of his name, and through its utterance opened a road for the nations to travel. His faith made him the father of the nations. And what are we to do, seeing that his election already comes first in his name? I ask you about your father's election, son of Abraham: what is it, and why is your race honored above all others? As a member of his household, reveal and explain to me his election and his name, and I will concede to you that you are walking rightly in his faith. If the Creator chose him alone out of everyone who ever lived, his love is not just, since he chooses one and rejects another. Why did he not choose another righteous man like him, so that [?] the company of the righteous would grow and wickedness would diminish? Yet righteous people did not come from the righteous man, so as to establish this. The wickedness of Abram's sons testifies that it is foreign to Abram. Let it be granted that he chose him however he chose him, since he has the authority to do so. Why did he change his name and call him the father of the nations? And if it is true that he becomes a father in keeping with his title, his election and his name are the basis of his fatherhood.

What do you say about Abraham, son of Abraham? How does your father become a father both to you and to the nations? Then the name Abraham gives you nothing more than others, for the nations too are his children, as it is written. Because of the nations, Abraham rose to a high rank. It is therefore clear that the nations were the reason for his greatness. Come then, son of Abraham, praise the nations, your relatives! For if they had not become your father's children, he would not have become great. Abram [?] is less than Abraham, however you may put it, just as his people is smaller than all the nations. If his fatherhood had remained confined to one people, his name would not have [?] in practice with the title he was given. Even the authority of the Lord who chose him would have been diminished, and the gods would have exercised greater dominion than he. And if only his own sons were his children, fatherhood over the pagan nations would have been turned elsewhere. If the Creator exercised dominion over his offspring, mute idols would have plundered what he had made. Only a small portion of what was his would have been given to him, while those without a voice would have been called lords. To those who are not gods, a multitude of nations beyond counting; and to the God of all, a small people, despised and enslaved! No, son of Abram! Do not belittle the one who established everything, for the nations that reject your unbelief belong to him. Your father's election shuts the door against your claims, for everyone who is a child of Abraham is a child of God. You have acquired nothing more than anyone else in the Creator's name, and you have no authority to shut the door against the nations. They are your relatives, you circumcised man who boasts of the mark in his flesh. Why do you not acknowledge kinship with Abraham's household? By the name of his own being, the Creator swore to your father and ours: “In you the nations will be blessed and become heirs to your inheritance.” Is the declaration of the one who swore by himself true, or is it not true? Have they come to be blessed, or is this perhaps still to come? If it has happened, then the nations have indeed become heirs to his inheritance. And if it has not yet happened, it certainly will—and what will you do? Acknowledge that it has happened: the books whose words are true bear witness.

And if it has not happened, then the truth within them is false. The nations have not become Abraham's children, you say. Then why is Abraham much dearer to them than to you? They have not been blessed through that declaration, “In you they will be blessed.” Then why are they inside while you are outside? Who turned their stubborn hearts away from error and made known to them the manifest truth of the Creator's name? Who laid the yoke of peace upon their strife and yoked them under the dominion of Abraham's Lord? Who became their counselor, advising them to hate evil, and placed in their hearts the good study of faith? Who occupied their minds with the study of love and took away from them the hateful bitterness of idolatry? Who opened for them the smooth road of the body's resurrection and taught them to walk in hope of the kingdom on high? Who uprooted the false structure that error had built and overthrew the temples that demons had adorned as their resting places? Who revealed to them that one Creator created everything, and accepted and assented to the written words [?] of his mouth? Who wrote for them a new book that they had not known? And now they meditate day and night on spiritual things. What power conquered the savage world and brought it in, confining it within the fortresses of the word of peace? Who subdued the four quarters of the earth in the name of one man? And now, instead of tribute, they offer him the sound of thanksgiving. Who yoked the West under the yoke of Jesus' name? And now it gives him fruits of praise without ever having enough. Who put the bits of faith into the East, so that it would no longer run wildly toward paganism? Who confined the harsh North within the fortresses of love, so that it would no longer wage a battle of injustice against righteousness? Who sowed good seed in the barren South? And now its bosom bears fruits of praise for the one who cultivated it.

Who abolished the borrowed names of those who are not gods and established on earth the honored name of the divine Being? Where are the mute idols that kinsmen fashioned? Look, they have vanished, and their memory has disappeared from people's mouths. Why have you, too, stopped having dealings with them, and why do you no longer sacrifice your sons and daughters as you did before? Why are you idle, no longer offering sacrifices on the high places? For there is never a time when the righteous are not recounting the charges against you. When did you ever stop offering idolatrous sacrifices as you have now, in your zeal against the nations? Your zeal is foolish, and it was not out of goodness that you stopped offering sacrifices. Otherwise, show me when you ever continued without sacrificial offerings. The killing you committed stopped you from idolatry against your will. And look, it has also turned the uncircumcised nations away, to your shame. Otherwise, tell me, if you have the ability to speak: how is it that idolatry has ceased while he is triumphant? Who put such zeal into human beings on earth that they choose death and hate life for the sake of the one you killed? How was a crucified man able to conquer creation? And who taught creation itself to obey his words? How did he conquer the world and its might through humility? And who, in turn, persuaded the world not to [?]? With what weapon did he wage battle against all the powers? For he possessed no visible weapon like earthly people. How were the lowly workers who accompanied him able to wage war against paganism and Judaism? I am speaking to you, son of Abraham, about your fellow countryman: how did he contend with weakness and hardship? It was your fellow countryman who did these things I am recounting to you, and the words of prophecy that were fulfilled in him bear witness. Is he of your people or not, O Jew? Did you crucify him in Judea or not? Make it clear and tell me. And if he exists, from whom does he come, and what is his lineage? And what is the reason for his crucifixion and his proclamation? Heaven and earth, which recount his glory, bear witness that he exists. You cannot deny the truth of his proclamation.

If he exists, this is what I asked you, and I ask again: by whose power was he able to conquer creation, if he himself is a creature? But if he does not exist, I ask you this as well: how has his name triumphed throughout creation if he does not exist? How can he speak when there is nothing of him at all? And how can we affirm that everyone believes in nothing? How is it that the nations have abandoned their gods and swear by the name of a man who, as you say, does not exist? If he was a deceiver, and you crucified him as a deceiver who had gone astray, how, once dead, did he lead those who know him astray through his death? Suppose he went astray, as you say—though far be it from him to have gone astray! Who would believe that a dead deceiver could lead everyone astray? Many have gone astray and led many others astray in their names, but after a time the teachers and their disciples disappeared. His supposed deception, for roughly five hundred years, has kept growing and putting out shoots in every land. Who has led people astray and had his counterfeit endure in his own likeness? And who has seized the Creator’s name without being exposed? No teaching endures on earth like his teaching, and no instruction gives growth like his instruction. Not even Moses, who established the law from the mouth of the Hidden One, could subject rebellious nations to his commandments. People did not worship the name of Moses or his writings, nor did they adorn temples for him on earth as they did for Jesus. Look, the Lord called him God among earthly beings, yet none among created beings called him by the name he was given. Look, he shone so brightly that people could not look at him; yet, though he was greatly exalted, no one says, “Glory to Moses!” The glory of the great Moses, Abraham’s son, has passed away, and no one praises the observances of the flesh. Otherwise, let every Jew who has something to say speak: where is Moses, and who among human beings has fulfilled his commandments? Show Moses’ glory openly, Israelite,

as the nations show the glory of the man you crucified. I acknowledge Moses’ greatness more than you do, but he is immeasurably less than the name of Jesus. He is less than Jesus, and again I say that he is far less—not in nature, but in divine rank. The swift spread of the proclamation of him testifies that he is greater than Moses: in its speed it has outstripped the sun and moon. Look, the sound of the proclamation of him thunders in every region, and people of every language weave the crown of his victory. Look, the Greeks honor the emblem of his crucifixion, and the barbarians too bear the yoke of his faith. And if you are unwilling to see with the visible senses, extend your mind to the four quarters and see his power. See how all languages cry out glory to his name and offer him gifts of love from their minds. Come then, Jew, compare what is mine with what is yours, and show whether your words have power as all mine do. Without quarreling, let us investigate the question between us, and let whoever loses give his hand to whoever wins. [?] your books, and let us argue with one another from them. Let every statement of mine and yours rest upon their words. I agree with you if you speak from what is written, and I do not reject the words of the Spirit of prophecy. Let Moses come, the firstborn of the divine writers, and among his letters let us investigate the question of this one who has come. What do you say, Moses, master of spiritual things? Reveal and explain to me the force of the meaning within your books. “A great prophet like me will arise from among mortals, and he is far greater than I, as high as heaven is above us. He is a great prophet, and his rank is greater than that of the prophets. Everyone is bound to submit to him as to the Lord.” Is Moses trustworthy or not, son of Abraham? Has his word been fulfilled, or is its time of fulfillment still to come? Has the prophet spoken of in Scripture arisen from your people, or not yet? Has this actually happened, or do you say it is still to happen? If it has not happened, as you think it is still to happen,

who is this who came and led you and the nations astray? For he did not lead only the nations astray, but you as well. This one who came and whom you killed led you astray first. The twelve voices that answered, belonging to men from among you, bear witness. Moses wrote that a great prophet would arise from among you, and through him the nations would be blessed and become children of Abraham. “By myself I have sworn,” the Lord said to righteous Abram, “that through you the uncircumcised nations will be blessed and become your offspring.” Who is this who blessed the nations in Abraham’s name? And how did it happen that the words became deeds? If he is not the one whose story the great Moses wrote, how does what he did resemble what is written? All the nations cry out together, “This is the one who has come!” Whom should we listen to—you alone, or the whole creation? The whole creation bears witness that he has come, since it has received him. You alone refuse to agree with the words of your own Scriptures. Otherwise, tell me, as a member of the household, when he is coming, and when the nations will become Abram’s relatives. Suppose he comes whenever he is to come, and the nations enter: why have you, a member of the household, gone out from your inheritance? Why have you been rejected like a wrongdoer for so long now, and why have priest, king, and prophet ceased to exist among you? Why have you been scattered to the four corners, as though in wrath, while the nations torment you with hard labor and kings with taxes? Why does no prophet arise from among you as in former times and tell you the reason for this subjugation? There was never a time when the voice of revelation ceased among you, either when you were in your own land or when the nations carried you into captivity. In Egypt there was Moses; in the land of Canaan, Joshua son of Nun; and among the Babylonians, one of royal descent and one of priestly descent. Nor did the spiritual beings ever stop or neglect helping you, until this one whom you killed came and restrained them. Why does that angel not rage against the firstborn and avenge your humiliation, as he did in the land of Egypt? Why does Michael, too, not fight against your adversaries,

as he fought against the ruler of the kingdom of Persia? Where is the love the heavenly beings had for your ancestors, since they do not help you as they helped generation after generation? There was never a time when they were so neglectful and silent as now, nor has your dispersion among the nations ever lasted this long. Look, for a little less than five hundred years you have been rejected and cast aside, and the longer it lasts, the further the delay imposed on you stretches. And if you say that your punishment has been prolonged because of your wrongdoing, look: your wrongdoing is no greater now than it was in former times. Compare and see that your wrongdoing is less than it was before, and your sin is smaller than what you committed in earlier generations. In the wilderness you provoked anger by worshiping the calf and through the daughters of Moab; and in the land of Canaan you went astray and acted foolishly with stones and wood. There was healing for all your ailments, and mercy was shown to you; but this illness has lingered with you beyond the usual course. Look, you are not sick with the worship of demons as you were before, nor are you sacrificing the fruit of your womb to unclean demons. Your illness has lingered, and perhaps there is no medicine for your wounds. Otherwise, show when you have ever remained without healing. In Egypt you lay sick with fever for two hundred years and more; then Moses came and drove suffering and injustice away from you. In Babylon, for seventy years, you were submerged as though in an abyss; then Daniel arose and prayed, and you came up according to the promise. Physicians walked with you in every land, and the medicine of the Spirit was never exhausted among your people. Why is there now no physician to bind up your wounds, and no herald to comfort you in your sorrow? Perhaps you will bring forward that written passage whose time has already passed: that priest, king, and the one who offers incense will cease to exist among you. But look, this was fulfilled in Babylon, when your orders ceased; and you returned and came up in the days of Cyrus with a great procession. In the days of Cyrus and under Zerubbabel you came up, as it is written. Or do you deny this too, as you are accustomed to doing? Then Zechariah and Haggai lied, and Malachi too!

And perhaps what Jeremiah composed was also a fabrication, and Ezekiel saw visions that were not true! Then Daniel did not go down to the land of the Babylonians either, nor did he pray and plead for the return at the end of seventy years! Did you return or did you not? Answer me as I have asked you. Has the Lord stretched out his hand a second time, or will he do so again? It is written that the Lord will act a second time, not a third. Whom should we believe—the prophecy or those who dispute it? This is the custom of Judaism: to deny in this way and, through contentiousness, reject the words of prophecy. You are accustomed to denying continually, son of Abraham. The calf bears witness: you fashioned it and then called it God. By God's power Moses delivered you from Egypt, but you attributed that deliverance to fashioned gold. And [?] you did not pour out offerings to it as to God? Why, then, did Moses test you in a furnace of water? Perhaps you will say, “Look, the Gentiles also do this, and by their deeds they insult the name of Jesus.” I accept the reply you make so cleverly, and I advise you to listen to my words with discernment. It was not because you sinned that I spoke with you, or that I speak now, but because you stand before the light and deny that it is bright. Otherwise, show me what is false in our teaching, which heaven and earth affirm as true, while you deny it. In this account I have recounted your offenses from the Scriptures, to show you your contentiousness against the truth. You are contentious and will not listen to those who instruct you. The righteous bear witness that you slaughtered them because they rebuked you. You fight against the plain statements in the Scriptures and are unwilling to accept the truth in them. You returned from Babylon, and this is clearer than the sun. Yet whenever people rebuke you, you put on a brazen face and say, “I did not come up.” You certainly returned! Why do you stubbornly deny it? Otherwise, who built you a house in the land of Judah? Zechariah and Haggai will cut down the obstinacy of your contentiousness,

for they put their hands to writing about the day of your return. Daniel too will enter into a just lawsuit against you, for he showed you beforehand the mystery of the coming of the king whom you rejected. Through the spirit of revelation he counted the weeks and arranged them, and at their conclusion he depicted the king’s suffering as in a picture. He declared that at his killing your city would be destroyed—or is that not written? It is therefore clear that, if it has not been destroyed, it is destined to be destroyed. If you have not killed the one whom you killed, his killing still lies ahead: you will kill him, and he will destroy your holy temple. It was not the compulsion of prophecy that forced your will, so that, whether you wished it or not, you would kill your king. It was not to kill your liberator that I called and urged you, but to expose the wickedness of your heart, for you thirst for blood. I did indeed see with a hidden eye that you were bent on bloodshed, and beforehand I depicted the wicked plot on the pages of the Scriptures. It was not I who called you the killer of your king, son of Abraham. Your prophets cry out like trumpets concerning the day of his killing. Your father Jacob, Judah, saw the suffering of his death and compared it to wine whose appearance glows in the eyes of those who see it. The son of Jesse too saw the tumultuous assembly against him and pronounced a sentence full of wrath against his killers. Isaiah marveled at his humility and his being sacrificed: he endured and remained silent and did not open his mouth at the time of suffering. Zechariah saw him stained with the blood of his covenants, releasing prisoners from within the pit where there was no life. Are these whom I have mentioned your prophets, or not? Did they speak by the Spirit, or from the inventions of their own minds? If they are truthful, accept the truth of their words. Otherwise, say that they are not truthful, and let the dispute cease. Either speak with me from their books, and I will answer you, or show me, and I will make room for your words. I accept all the utterances of prophecy and do not deal deceitfully with the meaning of their words. From them I learned to acknowledge the king who arose from you,

and they showed me how to walk in the way of faith in him. If your heralds revealed to me the mystery within your people, why are you jealous that I have become a member of your household? I did not choose for myself to become a fellow heir with you. They gave me a share with you. Why does that distress you? Your king freed me from slavery to the Evil One and death, and his love yoked me under his lordship. Why do you quarrel? He came to his own, and his own were unwilling to receive him. When he saw that they hated him, he chose your people for himself and rejected his own. Did he come to you or not? Tell the truth. Did he choose the nations for himself or not? Say how it really is. If he was not the one who came to you, whom did you do away with? And if he did not choose the nations in your place, why do they acknowledge him? That he came is clear, and nothing is clearer than this. That he chose the nations is attested by the nations and their gods. The nations that received him acknowledge that he came, while you deny it. Their gods surrendered to him, while you flee. What do you say about the worshipers and those they worship, when even the companies of heavenly beings proclaim his glory? Those who speak and those who are mute tell of him with voice and silence, while you alone keep your mouth silent from praising him. Wicked envy has blinded the eye of your discernment, and you are unwilling to see the light of his great glory. The wickedness of your inclination has made you blind and without understanding. Though you see, you do not see anything [?]. If you realized what blessings you are excluded from, perhaps you would call on heaven and earth to weep for you. If you were convinced of the judgment reserved for your insolence, perhaps you would weep night and day without ceasing. Blessings and punishments have been hidden from your mind, and you see neither present things nor things to come. Otherwise, who has become blind and deaf in a stupor like yours? You are rejected and remain quiet, without discerning why. You have become a stranger to heavenly and earthly beings,

and angels and human beings shun you, yet you feel no shame. You lie cast out like dung, and everyone tramples over your head. Yet you do not consider the reason for your own degradation. The path of heavenly beings to your people has been cut off, and you have not understood why they have ceased ministering to you. Divine revelations have ceased among your heralds, and no one brings medicine for your wounds, not even a poultice. If only you knew how to consider the depth of your abasement, and would groan over your lawless death! If only you could see your own ugliness—you are hideous—and feel ashamed, even a little, of your shameful deeds! If only you would listen to the correcting voice of those who instruct you, and open your mind so that the word of life might enter you! If only you understood the hidden things within the Scriptures, and saw that their power was fulfilled in this one whom you crucified! His cross toppled you from the authority of your exalted rank; he rejected you and cast you out of the inheritance of your ancestors’ house. His death, which is the source of life for the dead and the living, prepared a noose and double punishments for you. You are destined to enter into double punishments on the day of judgment, before that King whom you wickedly judged on earth. Without mercy he will inflict punishments for your wickedness—not because you killed him, but because you rejected his proclamation. In righteous judgment he will demand an account of the abuse his servants suffered at your hands—those whom he sent to you after his killing, but you did not listen to them. Through them he will punish your oppression, for you oppressed them greatly, and expose you before the eyes of angels and human beings. Response: Blessed is he who uprooted Zion, the crucifier, and planted the faithful Church within her borders.
On the Canaanite Woman.
Discourse for Tuesday of the Canaanite Woman. Response: Blessed is he who brought us back from captivity to the enemy through one of our own race, who conquered and made us victorious. My brothers.

The enemy of humanity roared unjustly against human beings and corrupted the image that bore the name of the divine Being. The murderer, drunk with envy against human beings, disturbed them with the foul smoke of his bitterness. The rebel clothed himself in furious jealousy against human beings, because those made of dust were unjustly [?] by the name of the divine Being. The [?] of humanity, drunk with envy against human beings, disturbed them with the foul smoke of his bitterness. The rebel clothed himself in furious jealousy against human beings, because those made of dust were unjustly called by the name of the divine Being. He armed himself with the weapon of deceit to destroy them, and with cunning sharpened his sword to [?] their blood. In every way he prepared himself for battle, to fulfill his bitter purpose through their deaths. He himself devised cunning schemes against their lives and buried deadly traps deep down to kill them. His thoughts skillfully wove a net of wickedness, large enough to hold a catch of human beings within its folds. On sea and dry land he spread his schemes like snares; he caught all nations and made them food for death. Through them he fought against their lives while they were unaware; he sent them out like spies and caught their companions. By their own hands he fought against their ranks [?] and overcame them; with the swords of their own thoughts he tore them apart. He cast the strife of his warfare into their thoughts and urged them to fight one another. They destroyed one another like strangers, without understanding, and tore apart the bodies of their fellow members as though they were not human. He taught them his bitter methods of warfare and instructed them in how to act wickedly. He wrote a deceitful book on the tablet of their minds, so that they would read wickedly according to his will. He saw that they were eager to meditate on his writings, and he set himself to perfect them in unseemly things. He settled among them and lived with them, and they with him. Although they loved him greatly, he hated them and corrupted them. It was not out of love that he enjoyed the company of earthly people, but to disturb their peace through his dealings with them. Under the guise of love he led them away from the truth, and with flatteries he deceived them through the confusion of his words. Demons ran wild and became shameless in people, and people in demons. The world went along, on sea and dry land, like a drunkard. The Creator saw that the Evil One had disturbed humanity’s peace, and he sent his command to bring humanity back to the peace of his name. He sent his command through a bodily messenger, so that through him he might speak a word of peace to humanity. On the parchment of the body he wrote the intention of his love, so that embodied beings might see the hidden through the visible. His will journeyed with visible limbs, and he came to them to teach them to return to him. He composed a body in writing, like a letter, and the power of his hidden being put its hand to it and sealed it with his name. He taught the body to read within itself the mystery of hidden things,

and to interpret the mysteries for its fellow beings. Like a commander, he armed it and sent it against the Evil One, so that through its victory its race might receive [?] of their debts. The embodied one went out with the divine will, and the hidden one raised his voice through the visible, and the demons trembled. The rebels heard a new voice crying out in a body. They shook and were bewildered by the novelty of this unfamiliar voice. The power of the divine Being roared through creation from a mortal mouth, and the ranks of the Evil One’s forces and ravenous Death trembled. The sound of the name of Jesus rang out on earth like thunder, and the demons wailed because they could not endure the greatness of his voice. With his voice alone he shook those filled with arrogance, and they began unwillingly to move out of their dwellings. Legion, the leader of their ranks, had heard the sound of his name. Anguish seized him, and he wailed and wept bitterly. The fame of the name of Jesus had gone out to every region, and peoples and townsfolk gathered to hear his word. A hidden summons gathered them to the harbor of his love, so that they might come and settle their minds in the peace of his name. They heard that by his word he drove out demons and healed pains, and they flocked from every [?] to receive medicine for their illnesses. A woman whose daughter had a demon dwelling in her went out to ask him for the medicine of the Spirit for the affliction caused by the demon. Her thoughts journeyed with her limbs after Jesus, and her impulses and senses began to turn toward the goal of his name. Who, then, taught the daughter of Canaan, the slave of slaves, to go out and ask the son of Abram for freedom of soul? Who revealed to the Canaanite woman, the daughter of accursed Ham, that the son of Shem could undo the seal imposed by the righteous man? Who told the worshiper of demons, whom the demons had defiled, that at the voice of Jesus demons depart from their dwellings? Who wrote a new book bearing the Creator’s name for the soul that had grown old in fellowship with demons, the enemies of truth? Who showed her, who was always traveling to the demons’ door, how to walk on the path of faith in one God? A hidden prompting mysteriously signaled to her within her mind: “Despise the worship of idols; believe and live!” It was he who girded her with faith as with armor, so that she might go out and fight the rebel who had taken her daughter captive. She girded herself with faith, hope, and love, and with the word of her mouth she cut down the Evil One as with a sword. Her mind put on faith like a coat of armor, and she grasped hope like a shield amid the [?] of her impulses. Her thoughts, together with her limbs, bent toward the goal of love, and she ascended and stood—stood in the lofty rank bearing the name of the pure. She armed herself spiritually with hidden armor, so that she could face the hidden battle of the Evil One’s forces. She knew that the enemy of humanity who was fighting her was hidden, and she prepared spiritual armor suited to his hidden nature. In secret she forged faith within her mind,

and gained strength to struggle with the mighty one. Her limbs girded themselves with faith, following her mind, and her senses and impulses raised their voice to ask for mercy. Mouth and mind together, with a humble voice, acquired the boldness of faith that cannot be defeated. Her mind cried out like a trumpet through her outward senses, and her mouth disclosed the anguish of her inward sufferings. Her mouth became an advocate for her impulses before the Judge, and the mute uttered choked sounds in place of articulate words. The daughter of the accursed one cried thunderously before the Son of the righteous one: “Have pity, Son of David, and free me from my enslavement to the captor! “Be gracious, Son of Abraham; stir up love for Canaan’s distress, and rescue my life from subjection to the Evil One’s slavery. “Our father’s father cursed my ancestors at the command of the hidden mouth, and yoked them beneath the Accuser’s harsh yoke. “Noah cursed our father, who impudently mocked and derided him, and blessed our father, who wisely honored and loved him. “The righteous man disciplined the insolent-hearted one as with a rod, and see, the lash has extended over his offspring until now. “Our insolence has suffered enough under our father’s lashes, and we have become slaves to the slave who rebels against the Maker. “Enough has the tyrant of wickedness enslaved the freedom of our souls, and our [?] mocked the ordered structure of human nature. “And if the offspring of insolent Ham are condemned to slavery, let them be slaves to the Son of righteous Shem, not to the tyrant. “Righteous Noah also declared this in his prophecy: that Canaan should serve Shem in slavery as his master. “Let us, then, repay you the debt of love as debtors, for you are of that lineage in which humanity’s freedom is inscribed.” You are the son of David and the son of Abraham, the son of Shem, the son of Noah. Free the slaves from the mighty one [?], so that they may be yours. I have heard of the promise of life that our father David received. Confirm his words through action, as befits you. The divine command sent you to bring peace to humanity. Fulfill in action the purpose of your coming; show [?] to those who doubt. I heard the report of you that spread throughout the land, and the rebels trembled. I came out to see the truth plainly through experience. I heard that people drive out demons in your authoritative name. I came to receive the good news of your name and carry it to the demons. A tyrannical demon entered and hid in my daughter's soul. It works secretly to sever her life from the living. Without pity it batters her body and bewilders her soul. Unless your command helps her, her life will come to an end. Send your command swiftly, like a messenger, to restrain the demon before it sets about shedding blood. Give me the seal of your authoritative name, and I will show it to him. Then he will be terrified like a woman in labor overcome by her pains. Write a letter, and let the power of your help sign it. When he sees it, he will no longer dare defy your command.” With a plaintive voice the daughter of Canaan pleaded.

And the one who knows everything kept her waiting, as though he did not hear. The disciples were astonished at her persistent cries and how much she pleaded. They approached and begged the physician to release her through his powerful help. “Give her the medicine of a word from your mouth, as you are accustomed to do, so that she may go and cure the affliction of the demon tormenting her daughter.” The master answered his disciples wisely: “I was sent only to heal the children of Jacob. I came out to seek the sheep that strayed from Israel, so that they might return and enter the fold of life of the Creator's name. For it is not fitting to give the bread of the freeborn children to the Canaanites, greedy dogs never satisfied with wrongdoing.” The daughter of Ham heard the master of the house call her a dog, and she gained hope that she too might live among the dogs. The Gentile woman saw the owner of the flock visiting his sheep, and she pressed to enter the fold of his gracious words. She saw that dogs too seek food, just like the heirs, and wisely asked the master of the house for nourishment. “Yes,” she said, “it is so, and you have spoken well, good master: I am a dog and am not worthy to be called an heir. Yes, the freedom of freeborn souls belongs to you, and sinners too are yours—the household dogs. Give the freeborn children the nourishment they deserve, and let the dogs live on the crumbs from their tables. Grant me that she may live among the dogs through your help, just as you give life to speechless creatures along with those who speak. Grant me to be worthy of a little crumb from your gift, for there is nothing among created things that does not live from the treasury of your love. Grant me to receive, along with the silent creatures, what I need to live, so that I may live by grace, like all the creatures your command nourishes.” Oh, the wisdom poured out by a heart that had wandered in error! It learned and taught how to speak wisely. Oh, the insights recounted by a mind occupied with sin! Instead of falsehood, it spoke truth before the one who knows everything. Oh, the mind that had grown old on earth doing wrong, yet longed for conversation with spiritual beings invisible to it! He did not see her for the first time and marvel at her as though he did not know her, for her faith was visible to him before she spoke. He was watching her before she gave voice to her petition, and he could hear the words of her mouth and her thoughts. He knew that he would heal her daughter's suffering with the medicine of his command, and it was clear to him that he would drive out the demon by his helping power. He was not testing her when she came and he did not heed her words. He wanted to show the truth of her love to those who did not understand. He did not reject and cast out of his flock the ewe that bleated [?] her love for the shepherd of all. He did not ignore her and remain silent because he begrudged her healing, but to give people the boldness to ask for mercy. Through boldness he also taught everyone to persist in seeking his help and not give up if they did not receive it quickly. By his delay, grace stirred the circumcised people to jealousy,

who boasted of their close relationship with the Creator's name. He shut the door against the chatter of insolent mouths that would say, “Look! He has turned away Abraham's children and visited the pagans!” He saw the hateful seed of their thoughts and uprooted it beforehand, before it could sprout and bear fruit. He knew that if he answered the daughter of Canaan, they would quarrel with him over why he had shown mercy to a worshiper of demons. He knew that the woman's love was genuine; [?] she would give up, however much he ignored her and did not answer her. For this reason he did not quickly signal an answer: he wanted to reveal her sincerity and rebuke the pride of those uncircumcised in heart. The sound of her words [?] was sweeter to him than [?], and he waited for her to go on singing her tender strains. By his delay he encouraged her steadfast heart to keep sounding its petition on the lyre of her mouth. Through her petition he stirred [?] to jealousy and taught the nations to see the light of faith in a daughter of darkness. Through her petition he stirred the people to jealousy and taught the nations to see the light of faith in a daughter of darkness. She came from the people whom demons had deprived of understanding. She danced toward him and, with her light, gladdened those in darkness. The truths of her soul [?] in her mouth like a torch, and it surpassed the sun's disk in brightness. Her voice became a herald in everyone's ears: “Come, all who are in need! Raise your voices and receive help!” The master of the house saw that she was eager to live and give life, and he made [?] her voice a guide toward the reward. Through the sound of her mouth he revealed the reward of things to come: this is how he enriches anyone who asks without giving up. “O woman,” he says, “very great is your faith! The whole world cannot compare with the steadfastness of your love. Your mind has gained great strength against the evil one, and you have not been overcome by the mighty one who fights against you. Your heart is wise, and your disposition is skilled in combat. No one knows better than you how to engage in battle. Your thought is shrewd, and your understanding is skilled at sound discernment. No bird has wings as swift as your movements. No athlete knows how to engage in battle as you do, nor does any archer aim at the target as your perseverance does. Because your love persevered and did not weaken [?] in its pleading, look, I am rewarding the labors of your faith. Because you persisted and knocked at the door of divine mercy, look, I am opening the door at your voice. Enter and rejoice! Because you, a suffering creature, counted yourself among the dogs, look, I am extending a crumb of mercy to satisfy your hunger. Because your disposition discerned wisely and called me Lord, look, I am enrolling you, who were lost, among the heirs. Because you desired and longed to become a ewe in the flock of my sheep, look, I am placing the seal of my lordship upon your mind. Because you believed and affirmed that my help was sufficient to drive out demons, look, I am confirming [?] through deeds the steadfastness of your soul. Look, I am inscribing [?] the helping power hidden in my words:

I stamp it with a hidden sign and give it to you. Go, show the unclean [?] demon the seal of my person. Look, he will be terrified, abandon his weapons, and flee naked. Go, tell him, ‘Jesus says: Leave our dwelling places, and go be tormented in a wasteland far from humanity.’ Go, announce his downfall to him who overthrows human beings: ‘Look, the lofty structure of [?] that you built on earth has been demolished.’ Go, explain to him the force of the meaning of my honored name: the name Jesus saves human beings and overthrows demons [?]. Go, tell him, ‘Look, the king has come out to reclaim what is his. Return the captives and give an account of those who [?].’ Await the decree for you, signed by the divine hand, and go show it to the tyrannical slave whose authority has been annulled. Indeed, the power of my utterances is reliable and does not prove false. Look, words have been matched by deeds, even while we are far away. Look, the demon has gone out before seeing the truth openly. He has abandoned his dwelling like a fugitive before a mighty warrior. Go, examine the truth of my words through experience, and receive proof of the great power of my glorious authority. Look, my will has pronounced sentence upon his wickedness, and he has begun tormenting himself in his frenzy. Look, he has heard the report that I am threatening his rebellion, and he has cried out and howled before the terrible scourge reaches him. Look, the body that he wore down with his bitterness is at rest, and the mind that he bewildered with his assaults has been restored.” From afar the king decreed battle against the rebel, and before him he cast down the bearer [?] of the writings. While the messenger waited for the king to put his hand to it, the deceitful one withdrew so that his fraud would not be publicly exposed. Who, then, taught the evil demon the plain truth, so that, while the arrows of judgment were still far away, he condemned himself? Who revealed his exposure to the utterly deceitful one, so that he hid himself from being publicly refuted before everyone? Who informed the crafty wolf, the destroyer of human beings, that the Son of David had come out to hunt him, just like his father? Who showed the deceitful fox the lion’s path, so that he slipped away at the entrance, lest the strength of his voice terrify him? A fearsome sign shook his heart and weakened his strength. Terror startled him; he abandoned peace and embraced turmoil. His mouth was full of weeping and lamentation as he went out, for he saw how harsh was the exile to which he was being sent. He had delighted in his vile deeds while dwelling among human beings. When he saw that they had driven him out, he despaired and concluded that there was no comfort. He saw that creation had been restored—Ham the slave, from his slavery [?]—and knew that the yoke of his oppression over mortals had been abolished. Through the Canaanite woman he learned how great his disgrace was: if a daughter of the accursed one had broken his yoke, who would take him seriously? Great was the anguish that seized the evil one in this affair:

A weak rib overcame his cunning schemes and trampled down his arrogance. Great is the wonder that she too struggled with perseverance, engaged the mighty one in combat, and was not defeated. The daughter of Ham fought a great battle against the rebel, hurling words of faith at him like arrows. O mighty one, overcome by the voice in which he had boasted! For he used to fashion the sound of his melodies in paradise. O warrior, defeated by the strength he had overcome in Eden! The hands he had bound through the eating of the fruit bound him. Through the eating of the fruit he bound Eve, who listened to his word; but the fruit of her own body turned against him and dashed him to the ground. With the fruit as his weapon, the guilty one triumphed and condemned Adam; but through the son of Adam he was defeated and exposed as no victor. On Eve’s lyre he played his melodies, which brought death as an inheritance; but through Eve’s daughter he heard the good news that death was abolished. In Eden he composed joyful songs like a victor; here he howled laments like one condemned. He groaned in bitter anguish when he heard everyone calling Mary blessed for the fruit she had borne. He was openly like a dead man, for Mary had brought him mourning, as he fled from the sound of the name ‘Son of David.’ He heard a woman’s voice crying out after Jesus: ‘Son of David, rescue the daughter of your household from the mighty one!’ Beautiful was her voice as she begged for mercy for her daughter; it was [?] against Satan, the enemy of humanity. At the sound of her sobbing, the heavenly assemblies were astonished, while the company of demons was dejected and mourned beyond measure. Whenever she uttered the name of Jesus with the tip of her tongue, the agitated demon was fiercely enraged. As she boldly pleaded for help, the demon groaned and wept over his downfall.
